content.content: Launching skill: alloq-implementation

1	# Refined prompt: KI-Angebotswerkstatt in `alloq-offer` — multiphase plan (Etappe 0 + 1)
2	
3	> Load `alloq-implementation` first in **every** phase, then `appkit-mantine-reference` before any `mn.*` component you have not used in this task, `reflex-state-and-architecture` / `reflex-testing-state` for states, `ai:building-pydantic-ai-agents` for the AI layer. Follow the test-first workflow and the definition of done of `alloq-implementation`. One phase = one reviewable PR. Do not start a phase before the previous one is green.
4	
5	## Task
6	
7	Build the AI-supported offer workshop described in `spec/ki-angebotswerkstatt.md` (German, 785 lines; read §5–§14, §17, §18 before each phase) **inside the existing package `components/alloq-offer`**. For an existing offer, an `offer_editor` adds customer sources (pasted text, EML, TXT, DOCX, PDF, PPTX, audio) and starts **one run that produces a complete first draft without further input**: extraction, a **User Story Map with simple stories (no acceptance criteria)**, the briefing, a scope proposal, all chapters of the bound Word template, rule checks plus AI review, and an editable DOCX draft in the existing QUO template layout. Afterwards the user only makes the decisions the AI must not make (confirm scope, resolve conflicts, confirm price) and may optionally refine the map on its own screen and the typed chapters in a Word-style document view before exporting a final DOCX.
8	
9	### UI design (binding)
10	
11	The UI **must follow the design "Kombination A + C – Entwurf in einem Durchlauf"** on the prototype canvas <https://claude.ai/artifact/SqvwnLbKttsfEL7XwnTcYX>. It has two clickable boards:
12	
13	| Board | File on the canvas | Screen in Alloq |
14	| --- | --- | --- |
15	| A + C · 1 Entwurf erzeugen und Story Map anpassen | `project/Werkstatt.dc.html` | Tab "Entwurf & Story Map" (Phase 1 start card, Phase 3 progress and decisions, Phase 4 map editor) |
16	| A + C · 2 Kapitel im Dokument: Kapiteltypen | `project/Kapitel.dc.html` | Tab "Kapitel" (Phase 5 document view, Phase 6 findings, Phase 7 export panel) |
17	
18	- Before building a screen, read its board (Artifact tool, action `read`, `url` above, `path` = the file in the table) and match its layout, texts, states and interactions. The boards are a layout and behavior reference, not code to copy: build with `mn.*` components, Alloq shell parts and `alloq_commons/theme.py` tokens.
19	- The first row of the canvas (concepts A, B, C) are earlier explorations. They are **not** the basis; where they differ from the A + C boards, the A + C boards win.
20	- Deviate from the boards only where Reflex/Mantine cannot do it the same way, and note each deviation in the phase's PR description.
21	
22	The plan covers spec Etappe 0 (template proof) and Etappe 1 (first end-to-end version) in detail. Etappe 2/3 are only listed under "Out of scope".
23	
24	## Decisions already made (do not re-ask)
25	
26	| Topic | Decision |
27	| --- | --- |
28	| Placement | Extend `alloq-offer` (import `alloq_offer`). New code lives in a sub-package `alloq_offer/workshop/`. Depends only on `alloq-commons` + appkit, never on `app` or other alloq packages. |
29	| UI stack | Reflex + `appkit_mantine` (not Next.js as the spec suggests). Rich text via `mn.rich_text_editor` (Tiptap wrapper in `appkit_mantine/tiptap.py`). |
30	| UI design | Design "Kombination A + C – Entwurf in einem Durchlauf" (see "UI design (binding)" above). |
31	| LLM | Azure OpenAI through **pydantic-ai** (`OpenAIChatModel` + `AzureProvider`) behind a narrow port. Tests use pydantic-ai `TestModel` / `FunctionModel` via `Agent.override`, never the network. |
32	| Access | Whole workshop (sources, transcripts, map, chapters, findings, exports) read **and** write only for role `offer_editor` (`OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE`, `@requires_offer_editor`). Offer list stays readable for all. No per-offer ownership in Etappe 1. |
33	| Storage | A `BlobStore` protocol; first implementation stores bytes in Postgres (`offer_blobs`, `LargeBinary`, deduplicated by SHA-256) so server and desktop share files. Azure Blob is a later adapter. |
34	| Template | `Templates/QUO-33441-N7R0Z4_Preisindikation MVP Referenzdatenbank Treystar .docx` (styles `berschrift1..3`, 8 tables, 2 content controls, no Jinja tags yet). |
35	| Plan depth | Etappe 0 + 1 detailed. |
36	| First draft | **One click, end to end.** Job `initial_draft` chains: extract → map → briefing → scope proposal → all chapters → checks → Word draft. No manual gate between stages (spec §9.1). Optional setting "Automatisch entwerfen, sobald neue Quellen nutzbar sind". |
37	| Story map | **Its own screen** (prototype board A + C · 1, based on concept A): graphical card grid, editable. It is **not** part of the document or the Word export. |
38	| Document | Word-style document view (based on concept C) made of **typed chapters**: `stories`, `prose`, `table`, `calc`. The `stories` chapter shows the written stories from the map, never the map graphic. |
39	
40	### Deliberate deviations from the spec
41	
42	- Spec §6.1, §6.3, §11.1, §13.1 and A24 put the story map at the start of the Word document. **Decision: the map stays in the app only.** The document and the Word export contain the written stories (key, title, one sentence, scope) through a `stories` chapter. Rule checks and acceptance tests are adjusted accordingly (Phase 6, Phase 8).
43	- Spec §9.1 says the initial generation creates map and chapters without manual approval; this plan extends it to scope proposal, checks and the Word draft in the same run. A scope proposal never counts as offered scope until the user confirms it (A25 still holds).
44	
45	## Context (found in the repo)
46	
47	- **Offer package today** (`components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/`): `entities.py` (89 l., `OfferEntity` table `offers`, `IndustryEntity`, `OfferStateEnum`), `models.py`, `repository.py` (`offer_repo`), `services/offers.py` (pure logic), `states/offer_state.py` (**578 lines** — do not grow it; workshop states are separate), `components/offer_*.py`, `pages.py` (`create_offers_page`, route `/offers`), tests in `components/alloq-offer/tests/` (one file per layer). Offers already carry `person_days`, `risk_buffer_days`, `production_cost`, `recommended_price` — reuse them as bound commercial values.
48	- **Access**: `alloq_commons/access.py` (`requires_offer_editor`, `requires_role` UI gate), `alloq_commons/roles.py` (`OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE` id 3). Background handlers cannot use decorators → inline role check inside `async with self` and list them in `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`-style lists of `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` (every new handler must be classified there; `alloq_offer` is in `OFFER_PACKAGES`).
49	- **Guards**: `tests/test_handler_authorization.py`, `tests/test_component_boundaries.py`, `tests/test_migrations.py` (one test per migration), `.claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py` (≤ 1000 lines; aim ≤ 400 per state).
50	- **Migrations**: head is `a2b3c4d5e6f7` (`alembic/versions/2026_10_22_offer_project.py`). Hand-written, `op.batch_alter_table`, named FKs/indexes, real `downgrade()`. Each new revision goes first in `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in `app/desktop/schema.py`. `alembic/env.py` must import the new entity module. **Never run alembic against the local profile** (it uses a shared remote DB) — the user applies migrations.
51	- **Async patterns**: only `@rx.event(background=True)` exists today (`alloq_dashboard/states/dashboard_states.py:170`, `alloq_project/states/project_validation_state.py:62`). `appkit_commons/scheduler/pgqueuer.py` is a cron-style scheduler, not a job queue — do not use it for workshop jobs.
52	- **Dependencies**: no LLM, docx, pdf, pptx or upload code installed. Add with `uv add --package alloq-offer <lib>` (CLAUDE.md: always `uv add`). `appkit_commons/ai/openai_client_service.py` exists but `openai` is not installed; prefer pydantic-ai's own Azure provider.
53	- **UI building blocks**: `alloq_commons/components/{shell.py (app_page), toolbar.py (window_toolbar, segmented, icon_button, primary_button), list_view.py, modal_layout.py}`, colors only from `alloq_commons/theme.py`, page popovers use `theme.PAGE_POPOVER_Z_INDEX`. `mn.dropzone` exists (unused so far). Static CSS goes to `assets/css/aq-*.css`.
54	- **Memory traps to respect**: list logic in big states → `rx.State, mixin=True`, never substates; keep DB code in place when splitting; `str(component)` escapes umlauts → assert on constants; `mn.number_input` on_blur sends formatted text; `rx.LocalStorage` lost on login; German names sort in Python, not SQL.
55	- **Docs**: feature docs live in `docs/features/` (see `offers.md`, `story-map.md`); diagram style per memory `docs-diagram-style`.
56	
57	## Target layout (inside `components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/`)
58	
59	```
60	entities.py / models.py          # split into entities/ and models/ packages once > ~400 lines
61	repositories/                    # BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession] + module singletons
62	storage.py                       # BlobStore protocol + DbBlobStore
63	jobs/                            # job entity helpers, claim/lease/retry, runner, handlers registry
64	extraction/                      # one parser per kind: text, eml, docx, pdf, pptx, audio
65	ai/                              # pydantic-ai agents, output schemas, prompt files, settings
66	services/                        # pure logic: map ops, story validation, scope, checks, diff, snapshot
67	content/                         # canonical content tree schema + editor HTML <-> tree converter
68	export/                          # template package loader, docx renderer, manifest
69	templates/quo_v1/                # chapters.yaml, rules.yaml, layout.docx (prepared copy)
70	states/                          # one state per tab; mixins for list logic
71	components/                      # sources, map, briefing, chapters, checks, export panels
72	pages.py                         # create_offer_workshop_page(sidebar) -> /offers/[offer_id]/werkstatt
73	```
74	
75	UI text German; code, comments, logs English; `logger.debug` default, no f-strings in logger calls, never log source content or prompts (spec §15).
76	
77	---
78	
79	## Phase 0 — Template proof and content contract (spec Etappe 0, §6, §10.3, §13)
80	
81	Goal: prove the QUO template can be filled with editable content before any AI work.
82	
83	1. Inventory the QUO DOCX with a small script under `scripts/` (headings, styles, tables, numbering, TOC field, content controls, header/footer). Write the result to `docs/features/offer-workshop-template.md` (chapter list, which parts are static, which become generated, style names to use).
84	2. Define the **template package** `templates/quo_v1/`:
85	   - `chapters.yaml`: stable chapter keys, title, level, required flag, **chapter type** (`stories | prose | table | calc`), type defaults (e.g. scope filter and grouping for `stories`, columns for `table`, bound fields for `calc`), guiding question, content rules, order. Default order per inventory: management_summary (prose), user_stories (stories, scope `angeboten` + `option`, grouped by activity), loesung (prose), leistungsumfang (prose), mitwirkung (table: Mitwirkung · Verantwortlich · Zeitpunkt), rahmenbedingungen, projektabwicklung, laufzeit (prose), verguetung (calc), annahmen_risiken (prose or table). Static legal chapters (Rechtlicher Hinweis, Rechtliche Bestimmungen, Bindefrist, Unterschriften) stay fixed template text. There is no map chapter.
86	   - `layout.docx`: a prepared copy of the QUO file with `docxtpl` placeholders / subdoc anchors per chapter; customer data removed.
87	   - `rules.yaml`: per-chapter required info and checks (used in Phase 6).
88	   - A Pydantic `TemplatePackage` model + loader with a `version` string; compatibility check (every chapter key has an anchor in `layout.docx`).
89	3. Define the **chapter content model** (`content/schema.py`, Pydantic, discriminated union on `chapter_type`):
90	   - `prose`: the **canonical content tree** — `paragraph` (inline runs: text, bold, italic), `heading` (levels 3–4 only inside a chapter), `bullet_list`, `ordered_list`, `table` (header row + rows of plain inline runs), `bound_value` (reference to a structured field, e.g. `offer.recommended_price`). Every block has a stable `block_id`.
91	   - `table`: `columns` (labels) + `rows` (cells of plain inline runs); no merged cells.
92	   - `stories`: **no stored text**, only settings — `scopes` (subset of `offen|angeboten|option|ausgeschlossen`) and `group_by` (`activity|slice`). Content is resolved from the bound map revision at render time (key, title, "Als … möchte ich …, um …", scope label). Never acceptance criteria.
93	   - `calc`: an intro paragraph (prose runs) + a list of `bound_value` rows (label + field reference).
94	   Anything else is rejected with a German validation message.
95	4. Word renderer (`export/docx_renderer.py`) using `docxtpl` + `python-docx`: one renderer per chapter type (strategy registry keyed by `chapter_type`), mapping to template styles; `stories` renders a heading per group and one entry per story (key + title bold, scope label, sentence); `calc` renders a two-column table of resolved bound values (unconfirmed values as visible draft placeholder, never invented); adds no external resources. Unsupported content raises a typed error (no silent loss). The story map graphic is never rendered.
96	5. Reference export test: render a fixture with one chapter of each type, long text, nested lists, a wide table, umlauts/special chars (`<>&„“€`), many stories across activities; assert structurally with python-docx (chapter order, headings, table cells, styles, story sentences, TOC field present). Write the file to `tmp_path` and keep one sample under `docs/` for manual Word check.
97	
98	Deps: `uv add --package alloq-offer docxtpl python-docx`.
99	Done: tests green; user opens the sample DOCX in Word and confirms layout (gate before Phase 3).
100	
101	## Phase 1 — Workspace foundation, storage and job runner (spec §8.6, §14.2, §15)
102	
103	1. Entities + one migration `2026_10_xx_offer_workshop_base.py` (down_revision `a2b3c4d5e6f7`):
104	   - `offer_workspaces` (offer_id unique FK → offers, RESTRICT because offers are never deleted; template_key, template_version, vision, roles JSON, map_revision int, story_seq int, doc_state `Entwurf|In Prüfung|Final`, created_by).
105	   - `offer_blobs` (sha256 unique, size, mime, data LargeBinary).
106	   - `offer_jobs` (offer_id, kind, status `queued|running|succeeded|failed|cancelled`, idempotency_key unique, payload JSON, input_revisions JSON, attempts, max_attempts, run_after, lease_until, error_class, error_message (technical text only), result JSON, timestamps). Index on (status, run_after).
107	2. `BlobStore` protocol (`put(bytes, mime) -> blob_id`, `get(blob_id)`, `delete`) + `DbBlobStore`; size limit from config.
108	3. Job runner (`jobs/`): `enqueue(kind, offer_id, payload, idempotency_key)` returns existing job for the same key; `claim_next()` uses `SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` on Postgres (plain select on SQLite tests); lease + heartbeat; bounded retries with backoff for transient errors; results of expired/cancelled jobs are discarded; model/parser calls run **outside** DB transactions. Handlers register by `kind` (registry pattern).
109	4. Worker: an async loop started via `app.register_lifespan_task` in `app/app.py`, enabled by config `offer_workshop.worker_enabled` (YAML + `__` env override), bounded concurrency. Desktop and server may both run it safely thanks to SKIP LOCKED.
110	5. Config section in `configuration/config.yaml` for workshop (limits, worker, Azure OpenAI endpoint/deployments, secret refs `secret:azure_openai_api_key`), loaded via appkit config pattern (`appkit-commons` skill).
111	6. Page shell: `create_offer_workshop_page(sidebar)` route `/offers/[offer_id]/werkstatt`, gated with `requires_role(…, OFFER_EDITOR_ROLE.name)`; tabs `Entwurf & Story Map · Kapitel · Briefing · Export` (sources live in the right panel of the first tab, findings in the chapter view, as in the prototype); entry from the offer inspector ("Werkstatt öffnen", offer_editor only). Opening creates the workspace lazily with the default template package. Without a draft the first tab shows the start card ("Entwurf aus N Quellen erzeugen", auto-draft setting, what the AI looks for) and never invented content (spec §5.1).
112	7. Tests: repository, job claim/retry/lease/idempotency (SQLite), state open/create workspace, authorization classification, migration test, `KNOWN_REVISIONS`.
113	
114	## Phase 2 — Sources and extraction (spec §5.2, §7)
115	
116	1. Entities + migration: `offer_sources` (offer_id, kind `text|eml|txt|docx|pdf|pptx|audio`, title, filename, mime, blob_id, sha256, version, replaces_id, status `hochgeladen|in Verarbeitung|nutzbar|teilweise nutzbar|fehlgeschlagen|manuell nötig`, status_detail, included bool, revoked_at), `offer_source_blocks` (source_id, seq, anchor JSON {page|paragraph|table|slide|shape|note|start_ms/end_ms|message_id}, kind, speaker, text, gap flag + reason).
117	2. Upload via `mn.dropzone` / `rx.upload` (type and size whitelist, no macros executed, macro-enabled Office types rejected) and a "Text einfügen" modal. Identical sha256 on the same offer → no new version, no new job. Replacing a file creates a new version.
118	3. Parsers (`extraction/`, one module each, pure `bytes -> ExtractionResult`):
119	   - pasted text / TXT; EML via stdlib `email` (subject, date, sender, message-id, quoted chain and signature detection, attachments become their own sources).
120	   - DOCX via python-docx (paragraphs, tables; anchors by paragraph/table index).
121	   - PDF via `pypdf` (pages; pages without text layer → gap "OCR nötig", not silently skipped).

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jens/Workspace/work/alloq/.claude/skills/alloq-implementation

# Alloq implementation

Alloq is a Reflex 0.10 app for resource and project planning. The generic skills
explain Python, Reflex and appkit in general. This skill is the Alloq layer: where
code goes in this repo, which guards it must keep green, and how Alloq tests look.
When the two disagree, this skill wins, because it describes the code as it is.

Stack: Python 3.14, uv workspace (`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac`), Reflex 0.10,
appkit-* (`appkit_mantine as mn`, `appkit_commons`, `appkit_user`, `appkit_ui`),
SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, Pydantic, Alembic, PostgreSQL in production and SQLite in tests.
UI text is German. Code, comments and log messages are English.

## Workflow for every task

1. **Search memory** for the feature words and for error text you see. Past sessions
   stored traps here (for example the mixin rule and the umlaut escaping in tests).
2. **Read the reference code of the layer you touch** before writing. The canonical
   slice is departments (see the architecture map). Copying its shape is faster and
   keeps reviews short.
3. **Plan the smallest diff.** Change the layers the task needs and nothing else. Do
   not move files, rename folders or refactor neighbours unless asked.
4. **Write or adjust the test first**, in the test file of the package you change.
   For a bug, first write a test that fails because of the bug. Run the touched test
   files once before changing code, so you know which failures were already there;
   report those instead of fixing them inside the same diff.
5. **Implement.**
6. **Run the gates**: `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test`.
   For a quick loop run only the touched test files with
   `uv run pytest <file> -q`, but run `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` whenever
   you add or change an event handler.
7. **Check file sizes**: `python .claude/skills/alloq-implementation/scripts/check_file_sizes.py`.
8. **Update memory** with any new trap or decision that the code itself does not show.

## Architecture map

Host app `app/` (entry `app/app.py`, admin pages `app/pages/*.py`, sidebar in
`app/components/sidebar.py`) plus uv workspace packages in `components/`:

| Package | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `alloq-commons` | shared kernel: entities, models, repositories, shared services, shared UI, `theme.py`, `roles.py`, `access.py` |
| `alloq-project` | projects and planning: `components/`, `services/`, `states/`, `pages.py` |
| `alloq-dashboard` | dashboard and portfolio: same layout, `models.py` for card payloads |
| `alloq-team` | team overview and employees: same layout |

Layers, in the order data flows (paths for departments under
`components/alloq-commons/src/alloq_commons/`):

| Layer | Where | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entity | `entities/department.py` | `class XEntity(Entity, Base)`, `to_dict()` with every field |
| Model | `models/department.py` | Pydantic read model plus `XCreate` write model with `Field` limits |
| Repository | `repositories/department_repository.py` | `BaseRepository[XEntity, AsyncSession]`, `model_class`, module singleton `x_repo` |
| Service | `<pkg>/services/*.py` | pure functions and dataclasses; DB loading kept in `*_inputs.py` or loader functions |
| State | `state/department_states.py` | `rx.State`, `rx.Field` vars, `@rx.event` handlers |
| Component | `components/department.py` | plain functions returning `rx.Component`, built from `mn.*` and shared parts |
| Page | `app/pages/departments.py` or `<pkg>/pages.py` | page factory `create_x_page(sidebar, route, title)` using `app_page` |
| Registration | `app/app.py` | call the factory with `sidebar()`; add a sidebar entry if needed |
| Migration | `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py` | hand-written, real `downgrade()` |

Dependency direction: feature packages import `alloq_commons` and appkit, never
`app` (`tests/test_component_boundaries.py` fails otherwise). Feature packages do not
import each other unless that import already exists. `app` may import everything.

`alloq_commons` has both `state/` (departments, roles) and `states/` (holidays). Put
new code next to its closest neighbour and do not merge the folders unasked.

Details, snippets and the background-load pattern: `references/architecture.md`.

## Where does this code belong?

- **Pure calculation** (scores, sums, sorting, grouping, labels) goes into a service
  function or a small dataclass, testable without a database. Examples:
  `alloq_dashboard/services/resource_path.py`, `alloq_project/services/project_sorting.py`.
- **Database reads and writes** go through a repository method, or a loader function
  such as `load_departments()` or `portfolio_inputs.py`. States do not build SQL.
- **UI state** (open dialogs, filters, toggles, selection) lives in the state. When the
  state file is large, put new vars and handlers into a mixin
  (`class XListState(rx.State, mixin=True)`), never into a substate; substates break
  tests that create the state on its own.
- **Rendering** goes into function components that read state vars. No logic beyond
  `rx.cond` / `rx.foreach` and formatting.
- **A value both the UI and a test need** (labels, messages, column lists) becomes a
  module constant, so tests can assert on it.

## Security: the handler authorization contract

Access levels (`alloq_commons.access`): admins may do everything; the project
manager role may read and edit every planning page (dashboard, planning, projects,
team) but not the administration; the employee role may only read planning and
projects. Page guards (`admin_only=True`, `editor_only`, `viewer_only`) only hide
the page. Event handlers run over the websocket for anyone with a session, so every
handler protects itself. `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` enforces this for all
states in the four packages. For each new or changed handler pick exactly one case:

1. **Reads or writes data in a planning package** (`alloq_dashboard`,
   `alloq_project`, `alloq_team`, `SidebarState`) → `@rx.event` then
   `@requires_editor` from `alloq_commons.access`. This is the default; the guard
   test rejects `@requires_admin` there.
1b. **Administration state** (`DepartmentState`, `RoleState`, `HolidayState`,
   `DatabaseAccessState`, listed in `ADMIN_STATES`) → `@requires_admin` from
   `appkit_user.authentication.decorators`.
2. **Read-only load the employee role may also run** → `@requires_viewer` from
   `alloq_commons.access`, and add the name to `VIEWER_HANDLERS`. It must not write.
3. **Only changes UI state** (open/close, set filter, toggle) → no decorator, add the
   name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]`. The test scans its source and the
   `self.` helpers it calls for DB markers (`get_asyncdb_session`, `_repo.`,
   `aggregation.`, ...), so a UI-only handler must not touch a repository or session.
4. **Background handler** (`@rx.event(background=True)`) → guard decorators are not
   allowed (they need the state lock). Check edit rights inside `async with self`
   through `_CardLoadMixin._run_card_load` (`_can_edit`) and list it in
   `INLINE_ADMIN_CHECK`.

Edit controls in the planning UI go inside `editor_only(...)` or use
`disabled=~CAN_EDIT`; `admin_only(...)` is for administration only.

Handlers defined in a mixin are listed under the concrete state that mixes it in
(`TeamState`, `ProjectState`, `PlanningStore`), because the test skips mixins.
Remove allowlist entries when you delete or guard a handler; stale entries fail too.
Run the test after every handler change.

## Style that ruff does not catch

- German UI strings, including toasts: `rx.toast.error("Fehler beim Erstellen der
  Abteilung.", position="top-right")`. English for code, comments, docstrings, logs.
- `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` per module; `%s` arguments, never f-strings
  in log calls; `logger.exception(...)` in the final `except Exception` of a handler.
- Handler error shape: `ValidationError` → German hint, `IntegrityError` → duplicate
  message, `Exception` → `logger.exception` plus a generic German error toast.
- Colors, radii and shadows only from `alloq_commons.theme` (`theme.CARD`,
  `theme.TEXT_MUTED`, `theme.BLUE[6]`, ...). The theme is macOS blue; ignore the old
  teal design artifact.
- Use `mn.*` components. Load `appkit-mantine-reference` before using one you have
  not used in this task; its props are not in your training data.
- HTML attributes on `mn` inputs: `max_length=20` turns into CSS and limits nothing.
  Use `custom_attrs={"maxLength": 20}` for the browser limit, and keep the real check
  in the write model (`Field(max_length=20)`).
- State vars: `name: rx.Field[T] = rx.field(default)`; lists use
  `rx.field(default_factory=list)`. Type hints on every function, including tests.
- Prefer shared parts over new ones: `modal_form_layout`, `modal_footer`,
  `delete_dialog`, `toolbar_search`, `primary_button`, `section`, `app_page`,
  `window_toolbar`, `de_number`.

## Testing standards

Coverage must stay at 80 % or more (branch coverage, `fail_under = 80`). Put tests in
the package that owns the code: `components/<pkg>/tests/test_<feature>.py`. App-level
tests and the guards live in `tests/`.

- **Entity/model**: `to_dict()` keys, `XCreate` rejects bad input.
- **Service**: plain unit tests with hand-built inputs, no mocks needed.
- **State**: create the state directly, patch `MODULE.x_repo` and
  `MODULE.get_asyncdb_session`, fake the admin with `_as_admin`, and drive handlers
  with `_run`, which returns the toast text. Copy the helpers from
  `components/alloq-commons/tests/test_departments.py`.
- **Component**: render with `str(component())` and assert on var names or module
  constants. `str()` escapes umlauts (`ä` becomes `\u00e4`), so assert on the constant.
- **Migration with data changes**: add a test in `tests/test_migrations.py` that runs
  the migration offline on SQLite.

Recipes and snippets: `references/testing.md`.

## Definition of done

- [ ] Test written first; new behaviour and the bug case are covered
- [ ] `task format && task lint && task typecheck && task test` all green
- [ ] `tests/test_handler_authorization.py` and `tests/test_component_boundaries.py` green
- [ ] Every new handler has its guard or its allowlist entry
- [ ] New migration is hand-written, uses `op.batch_alter_table` for column changes,
      has a real `downgrade()`, and its revision is added to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in
      `app/desktop/schema.py`
- [ ] No touched file grew past 1000 lines; files already over it did not grow
      without reason (see `references/pitfalls.md`)
- [ ] German UI text, theme tokens, no `print`, no f-strings in logs
- [ ] Memory updated with new traps or decisions

Per change type (new field, new handler, new page, new service, bug fix):
`references/checklists.md`. Known traps: `references/pitfalls.md`.

## Which generic skill for what

| Need | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| Python style, logging, typing, design patterns | `python-coding`, `python-clean-code` |
| Reflex state design, events, background tasks | `reflex-state-and-architecture`, `reflex-docs` |

# Checklists per change type

Use the list that matches the task. Each step names the file to touch, so you can
see quickly what a complete change looks like.

## New field on an existing entity

1. Entity `commons/entities/<x>.py`: `Mapped[...] = mapped_column(...)`; optional
   fields are `Mapped[str | None]` with `nullable=True`.
2. `to_dict()` in the same entity: add the key. Read models are built from it, so a
   missing key silently drops the value.
3. Read model `commons/models/<x>.py`: field with a default (`""`, `0`, `None`).
4. Write model `XCreate`: field with `Field(...)` limits that match the column.
5. Form parsing in the state (`_x_from_form`) and the create/update handlers: set
   the new attribute on the entity.
6. Component: form field (`mn.text_input(name=..., label="<German>", ...)` with
   `default_value` for edit mode and `custom_attrs={"maxLength": N}` for a length
   limit), table column and header if it should show. Keep the label in a module
   constant so tests can assert on it.
7. Migration `alembic/versions/YYYY_MM_DD_<topic>.py`: hand-written,
   `with op.batch_alter_table("<table>") as batch_op: batch_op.add_column(...)`,
   `downgrade()` drops it. `down_revision` is the current head; prepend the new
   revision to `KNOWN_REVISIONS` in `app/desktop/schema.py`.
8. Desktop app reads with the same entities, so no extra desktop code is needed
   unless `app/desktop/` code lists columns explicitly (grep for the table name).
9. Tests: `to_dict` key, write model limits, handler stores the value, component
   renders the field.

## New entity

Everything above, plus: repository with singleton, exports in `entities/__init__.py`,
`models/__init__.py`, `repositories/__init__.py`, `op.create_table` with
`created`/`updated` columns like `2026_10_18_departments.py`, and a test file.

## New state handler

1. Decide the guard (SKILL.md, security section). Default is `@rx.event` +
   `@requires_editor`; administration states use `@requires_admin`.
2. UI-only: add the name to `UI_ONLY_HANDLERS["<ConcreteState>"]` in
   `tests/test_handler_authorization.py`, sorted like its neighbours. In a mixin,
   use the concrete state's name.
3. Keep data access in a repository or loader; the handler calls it inside
   `async with get_asyncdb_session() as session:`.
4. German toast texts; `logger.exception` in the last `except`.
5. Tests: one per path (success, validation, not found, error).
6. Run `uv run pytest tests/test_handler_authorization.py -q`.

## New computed var or filter

1. `@rx.var` method on the state or mixin, returning a typed value.
2. If it needs a new UI-only setter, follow "New state handler".
3. Test by setting vars on a bare state and reading the var.

## New page

1. Components in the feature package (`<pkg>/components/<x>.py`).
2. Page factory: admin page in `app/pages/<x>.py`, feature page in `<pkg>/pages.py`;
   `app_page(route=..., title="<German>", sidebar=sidebar, toolbar=window_toolbar(...),
   admin_only=True, on_load=[XState.load_x])`.
3. Register in `app/app.py` (`create_x_page(sidebar())`) and add
   `("/route", "<German label>", "<lucide icon>")` to `PLANNING_ITEMS` or
   `ADMIN_ITEMS` in `app/components/sidebar.py`.
4. Tests: render tests for the new components in the feature package;
   `tests/test_sidebar.py::...::test_renders_navigation_entries` already loops over
   all sidebar items, so a new entry is covered once it renders.

## New service

1. Pure function or frozen dataclass in `<pkg>/services/<topic>.py`; input is rows or
   models, output is a model or dataclass. No session inside the pure part.
2. Loader in a separate function or `*_inputs.py` module if it reads the DB.
3. A DB-reaching function name that a UI-only handler might call must not be added
   to a UI-only handler; the guard test checks `aggregation.` and similar markers.
4. Tests: plain unit tests for the pure part; patched session for the loader.

## Bug fix

1. Reproduce with a failing test in the test file of the code that is wrong. Name it
   after the expected behaviour (`test_drill_down_score_clamps_impact`).
2. Fix at the source of the wrong value, not where it shows. If two places compute
   the same thing, make one call the other instead of copying the formula.
3. Keep the diff small, even in files over 1000 lines; note the file size in your
   summary instead of refactoring unasked.
4. Run the touched test file, then the full gates.

cd /Users/jens/Workspace/work/alloq && export UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=.venv.mac && mkdir -p scripts && cat > scripts/inventory_docx.py <<'EOF'
"""Print an inventory of a DOCX template: paragraphs, styles, tables, fields."""

import sys
from pathlib import Path

from docx import Document
from docx.oxml.ns import qn


def main(path: str) -> None:
    doc = Document(path)
    body = doc.element.body
    index = 0
    for child in body.iterchildren():
        tag = child.tag.split("}")[1]
        if tag == "p":
            para = doc.paragraphs[index] if index < len(doc.paragraphs) else None
            index += 1
            style = child.find(qn("w:pPr") + "/" + qn("w:pStyle"))
            style_id = style.get(qn("w:val")) if style is not None else "-"
            text = "".join(t.text or "" for t in child.iter(qn("w:t")))
            fields = [i.text for i in child.iter(qn("w:instrText"))]
            sdt = len(list(child.iter(qn("w:sdt"))))
            print(f"P [{style_id}] {text[:90]!r} fields={fields} sdt={sdt}")
            del para
        elif tag == "tbl":
            rows = child.findall(qn("w:tr"))
            first = ["".join(t.text or "" for t in c.iter(qn("w:t"))) for c in rows[0].findall(qn("w:tc"))]
            print(f"TABLE rows={len(rows)} first_row={first}")
        elif tag == "sdt":
            print("SDT block")
    for section in doc.sections:
        print("HEADER", [p.text for p in section.header.paragraphs if p.text])
        print("FOOTER", [p.text for p in section.footer.paragraphs if p.text])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else str(Path("Templates").glob("QUO*.docx").__next__()))
EOF
uv run python scripts/inventory_docx.py 2>&1 | head -150

"""Build workshop/templates/quo_v1/layout.docx from the QUO customer template.

Keeps the cover and the static legal tail, removes the generated chapters and
replaces customer data by docxtpl placeholders. Run from the repository root.
"""

import copy
import glob
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from docx import Document
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn

TARGET = Path(
    "components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/templates/quo_v1/layout.docx"
)
ANCHOR = "[[KAPITEL]]"
FIRST_GENERATED = "Management Summary"
FIRST_STATIC_TAIL = "Rechtliche Bestimmungen"

COVER_PLACEHOLDERS = {
    "MVP Referenzdatenbank": "{{ project_title }}",
    "TREYSTA Ingenieure Holding GmbH": "{{ customer_name }}",
    "Kurfürstendamm 29": "{{ customer_street }}",
    "10719 Berlin": "{{ customer_city }}",
    "- Im Folgenden „Treysta” oder „Auftraggeber“ genannt -": (
        "- Im Folgenden „{{ customer_short }}“ oder „Auftraggeber“ genannt -"
    ),
    "Leipzig, 19. Oktober 2026": "Leipzig, {{ offer_date }}",
    "Quote ID: QUO-33441-N7R0Z4": "Quote ID: {{ quote_id }}",
    "Der Auftragnehmer hält sich bis einschließlich zum 30.November.2026 an dieses Angebot gebunden.": (
        "Der Auftragnehmer hält sich bis einschließlich zum {{ validity_date }} an dieses Angebot gebunden."
    ),
}


def text_of(elem) -> str:
    return "".join(t.text or "" for t in elem.iter(qn("w:t")))


def set_text(paragraph, text: str) -> None:
    runs = paragraph.findall(qn("w:r"))
    first = runs[0]
    for run in runs[1:]:
        paragraph.remove(run)
    for t in first.findall(qn("w:t")):
        first.remove(t)
    node = OxmlElement("w:t")
    node.text = text
    node.set("{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space", "preserve")
    first.append(node)


def heading1_index(kids, title: str) -> int:
    for i, kid in enumerate(kids):
        style = kid.find(qn("w:pPr") + "/" + qn("w:pStyle"))
        if (
            kid.tag == qn("w:p")
            and style is not None
            and style.get(qn("w:val")) == "berschrift1"
            and text_of(kid).strip() == title
        ):
            return i
    raise SystemExit(f"heading not found: {title}")


def toc_paragraph(doc: Document):
    title = doc.element.makeelement(qn("w:p"), {})
    ppr = OxmlElement("w:pPr")
    style = OxmlElement("w:pStyle")
    style.set(qn("w:val"), "berschriftohneNummerierung")
    ppr.append(style)
    title.append(ppr)
    run = OxmlElement("w:r")
    t = OxmlElement("w:t")
    t.text = "Inhaltsverzeichnis"
    run.append(t)
    title.append(run)

    para = OxmlElement("w:p")
    for kind, payload in (
        ("begin", None),
        ("instr", ' TOC \\o "1-3" \\h \\z \\u '),
        ("separate", None),
        ("text", "Inhaltsverzeichnis wird beim Öffnen in Word aktualisiert."),
        ("end", None),
    ):
        r = OxmlElement("w:r")
        if kind == "instr":
            node = OxmlElement("w:instrText")
            node.text = payload
            node.set("{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space", "preserve")
        elif kind == "text":
            node = OxmlElement("w:t")
            node.text = payload
        else:
            node = OxmlElement("w:fldChar")
            node.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), kind)
        r.append(node)
        para.append(r)
    return title, para


def main() -> None:
    source = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else glob.glob("Templates/QUO*.docx")[0]
    doc = Document(source)
    body = doc.element.body
    kids = list(body.iterchildren())
    start = heading1_index(kids, FIRST_GENERATED)
    end = heading1_index(kids, FIRST_STATIC_TAIL)
    for kid in kids[start:end]:
        body.remove(kid)

    anchor = copy.deepcopy(kids[start - 2])
    for child in list(anchor):
        anchor.remove(child)
    run = OxmlElement("w:r")
    node = OxmlElement("w:t")
    node.text = ANCHOR
    run.append(node)
    anchor.append(run)
    toc_title, toc = toc_paragraph(doc)
    tail_first = kids[end]
    for elem in (toc_title, toc, anchor):
        tail_first.addprevious(elem)

    for paragraph in body.iter(qn("w:p")):
        replacement = COVER_PLACEHOLDERS.get(text_of(paragraph).strip())
        if replacement is not None:
            set_text(paragraph, replacement)
    for table in body.iter(qn("w:tbl")):
        for paragraph in table.iter(qn("w:p")):
            if text_of(paragraph).strip() == "TREYSTA Ingenieure Holding GmbH":
                set_text(paragraph, "{{ customer_name }}")

    TARGET.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    doc.save(TARGET)
    print(f"written {TARGET}")  # noqa: T201


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

"""Build workshop/templates/quo_v1/layout.docx from the QUO customer template.

Keeps the cover and the static legal tail, removes the generated chapters and
replaces customer data by docxtpl placeholders. Run from the repository root.
"""

import copy
import glob
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from docx import Document
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn

TARGET = Path(
    "components/alloq-offer/src/alloq_offer/workshop/templates/quo_v1/layout.docx"
)
ANCHOR = "[[KAPITEL]]"
FIRST_GENERATED = "Management Summary"
FIRST_STATIC_TAIL = "Rechtliche Bestimmungen"

COVER_PLACEHOLDERS = {
    "MVP Referenzdatenbank": "{{ project_title }}",
    "TREYSTA Ingenieure Holding GmbH": "{{ customer_name }}",
    "Kurfürstendamm 29": "{{ customer_street }}",
    "10719 Berlin": "{{ customer_city }}",
    "- Im Folgenden „Treysta” oder „Auftraggeber“ genannt -": (
        "- Im Folgenden „{{ customer_short }}“ oder „Auftraggeber“ genannt -"
    ),
    "Leipzig, 19. Oktober 2026": "Leipzig, {{ offer_date }}",
    "Quote ID: QUO-33441-N7R0Z4": "Quote ID: {{ quote_id }}",
    "Der Auftragnehmer hält sich bis einschließlich zum 30.November.2026 an dieses Angebot gebunden.": (
        "Der Auftragnehmer hält sich bis einschließlich zum {{ validity_date }} an dieses Angebot gebunden."
    ),
}


def text_of(elem) -> str:
    return "".join(t.text or "" for t in elem.iter(qn("w:t")))


def set_text(paragraph, text: str) -> None:
    runs = paragraph.findall(qn("w:r"))
    first = runs[0]
    for run in runs[1:]:
        paragraph.remove(run)
    for t in first.findall(qn("w:t")):
        first.remove(t)
    node = OxmlElement("w:t")
    node.text = text
    node.set("{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space", "preserve")
    first.append(node)


def heading1_index(kids, title: str) -> int:
    for i, kid in enumerate(kids):
        style = kid.find(qn("w:pPr") + "/" + qn("w:pStyle"))
        if (
            kid.tag == qn("w:p")
            and style is not None
            and style.get(qn("w:val")) == "berschrift1"
            and text_of(kid).strip() == title
        ):
            return i
    raise SystemExit(f"heading not found: {title}")


def toc_paragraph(doc: Document):
    title = doc.element.makeelement(qn("w:p"), {})
    ppr = OxmlElement("w:pPr")
    style = OxmlElement("w:pStyle")
    style.set(qn("w:val"), "berschriftohneNummerierung")
    ppr.append(style)
    title.append(ppr)
    run = OxmlElement("w:r")
    t = OxmlElement("w:t")
    t.text = "Inhaltsverzeichnis"
    run.append(t)
    title.append(run)

    para = OxmlElement("w:p")
    for kind, payload in (
        ("begin", None),
        ("instr", ' TOC \\o "1-3" \\h \\z \\u '),
        ("separate", None),
        ("text", "Inhaltsverzeichnis wird beim Öffnen in Word aktualisiert."),
        ("end", None),
    ):
        r = OxmlElement("w:r")
        if kind == "instr":
            node = OxmlElement("w:instrText")
            node.text = payload
            node.set("{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space", "preserve")
        elif kind == "text":
            node = OxmlElement("w:t")
            node.text = payload
        else:
            node = OxmlElement("w:fldChar")
            node.set(qn("w:fldCharType"), kind)
        r.append(node)
        para.append(r)
    return title, para


def main() -> None:
    source = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else glob.glob("Templates/QUO*.docx")[0]
    doc = Document(source)
    body = doc.element.body
    kids = list(body.iterchildren())
    start = heading1_index(kids, FIRST_GENERATED)
    end = heading1_index(kids, FIRST_STATIC_TAIL)
    for kid in kids[start:end]:
        body.remove(kid)

    anchor = copy.deepcopy(kids[start - 2])
    for child in list(anchor):
        anchor.remove(child)
    run = OxmlElement("w:r")
    node = OxmlElement("w:t")
    node.text = ANCHOR
    run.append(node)
    anchor.append(run)
    toc_title, toc = toc_paragraph(doc)
    tail_first = kids[end]
    for elem in (toc_title, toc, anchor):
        tail_first.addprevious(elem)

    for paragraph in body.iter(qn("w:p")):
        replacement = COVER_PLACEHOLDERS.get(text_of(paragraph).strip())
        if replacement is not None:
            set_text(paragraph, replacement)
    for table in body.iter(qn("w:tbl")):
        for paragraph in table.iter(qn("w:p")):
            if text_of(paragraph).strip() == "TREYSTA Ingenieure Holding GmbH":
                set_text(paragraph, "{{ customer_name }}")

    TARGET.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    doc.save(TARGET)
    print(f"written {TARGET}")  # noqa: T201


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF

"""Typed chapter content model of the offer workshop.

A chapter holds one of four content types. ``prose`` is the canonical block
tree, ``table`` a plain grid, ``stories`` only settings (the text is resolved
from the story map when rendering) and ``calc`` bound commercial values.
Anything outside this model is rejected with a German message.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError, field_validator

STORY_SCOPES: tuple[str, ...] = ("offen", "angeboten", "option", "ausgeschlossen")
GROUP_BY_VALUES: tuple[str, ...] = ("activity", "slice")

BOUND_FIELDS: dict[str, str] = {
    "offer.person_days": "Personentage",
    "offer.risk_buffer_days": "Risikopuffer (Personentage)",
    "offer.production_cost": "Herstellkosten",
    "offer.recommended_price": "Empfohlener Preis",
    "workspace.currency": "Währung",
    "workspace.validity_date": "Bindefrist",
}


class ContentValidationError(ValueError):
    """Chapter content violates the content model; messages are German."""

    def __init__(self, messages: list[str]) -> None:
        super().__init__("; ".join(messages))
        self.messages = messages


def _new_block_id() -> str:
    return uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]


class Run(BaseModel):
    text: str
    bold: bool = False
    italic: bool = False


Inline = list[Run]


class _Block(BaseModel):
    block_id: str = Field(default_factory=_new_block_id)


class Paragraph(_Block):
    type: Literal["paragraph"] = "paragraph"
    runs: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)


class Heading(_Block):
    type: Literal["heading"] = "heading"
    level: Literal[3, 4] = 3
    runs: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)


class BulletList(_Block):
    type: Literal["bullet_list"] = "bullet_list"
    items: list[Inline] = Field(default_factory=list)


class OrderedList(_Block):
    type: Literal["ordered_list"] = "ordered_list"
    items: list[Inline] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TableBlock(_Block):
    type: Literal["table"] = "table"
    header: list[Inline] = Field(default_factory=list)
    rows: list[list[Inline]] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @field_validator("rows")
    @classmethod
    def _rows_match_header(
        cls, rows: list[list[Inline]], info: object
    ) -> list[list[Inline]]:
        header = getattr(info, "data", {}).get("header", [])
        if any(len(row) != len(header) for row in rows):
            raise ValueError("Jede Tabellenzeile braucht genau so viele Zellen wie die Kopfzeile.")
        return rows


class BoundValue(_Block):
    type: Literal["bound_value"] = "bound_value"
    field: str

    @field_validator("field")
    @classmethod
    def _known_field(cls, value: str) -> str:
        if value not in BOUND_FIELDS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unbekannter Kalkulationswert: {value}")
        return value


ProseBlock = Annotated[
    Paragraph | Heading | BulletList | OrderedList | TableBlock | BoundValue,
    Field(discriminator="type"),
]


class ProseContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["prose"] = "prose"
    blocks: list[ProseBlock] = Field(default_factory=list)


class TableContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["table"] = "table"
    columns: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    rows: list[list[Inline]] = Field(default_factory=list)

    @field_validator("rows")
    @classmethod
    def _rows_match_columns(
        cls, rows: list[list[Inline]], info: object
    ) -> list[list[Inline]]:
        columns = getattr(info, "data", {}).get("columns", [])
        if any(len(row) != len(columns) for row in rows):
            raise ValueError("Jede Tabellenzeile braucht genau so viele Zellen wie Spalten.")
        return rows


class StoriesContent(BaseModel):
    """Settings only; stories are resolved from the map revision at render time."""

    chapter_type: Literal["stories"] = "stories"
    scopes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=lambda: ["angeboten", "option"])
    group_by: Literal["activity", "slice"] = "activity"

    @field_validator("scopes")
    @classmethod
    def _known_scopes(cls, scopes: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        unknown = [scope for scope in scopes if scope not in STORY_SCOPES]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"Unbekannter Umfang: {', '.join(unknown)}")
        return scopes


class CalcRow(BaseModel):
    label: str
    field: str

    @field_validator("field")
    @classmethod
    def _known_field(cls, value: str) -> str:
        if value not in BOUND_FIELDS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unbekannter Kalkulationswert: {value}")
        return value


class CalcContent(BaseModel):
    chapter_type: Literal["calc"] = "calc"
    intro: Inline = Field(default_factory=list)
    rows: list[CalcRow] = Field(default_factory=list)


ChapterContent = Annotated[
    ProseContent | TableContent | StoriesContent | CalcContent,
    Field(discriminator="chapter_type"),
]

CHAPTER_TYPES: tuple[str, ...] = ("prose", "table", "stories", "calc")


def plain_text(runs: Inline) -> str:
    return "".join(run.text for run in runs)


def parse_content(data: dict) -> ProseContent | TableContent | StoriesContent | CalcContent:
    """Validate raw JSON content; raise ``ContentValidationError`` in German."""
    from pydantic import TypeAdapter

    chapter_type = data.get("chapter_type") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
    if chapter_type not in CHAPTER_TYPES:
        raise ContentValidationError(["Unbekannter Kapiteltyp."])
    try:
        return TypeAdapter(ChapterContent).validate_python(data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        messages = [_german(err) for err in exc.errors()]
        raise ContentValidationError(messages) from exc


def _german(error: dict) -> str:
    message = str(error.get("msg", ""))
    if message.startswith("Value error, "):
        return message.removeprefix("Value error, ")
    location = ".".join(str(part) for part in error.get("loc", ()))
    if error.get("type") == "union_tag_invalid":
        return f"Nicht unterstützter Inhaltsbaustein ({location})."
    return f"Ungültiger Inhalt ({location})."

        match block:
            case Paragraph():
                writer.paragraph(block.runs)
            case Heading():
                writer.heading(_plain(block.runs), max(block.level, inner_min))
            case BulletList():
                for item in block.items:
                    writer.paragraph(item, BULLET_STYLE)
            case OrderedList():
                for item in block.items:
                    writer.paragraph(item, ORDERED_STYLE)
            case TableBlock():
                writer.table(block.header, block.rows)
            case BoundValue():
                label = BOUND_FIELDS[block.field]
                writer.paragraph(
                    _text(f"{label}: {_resolve(ctx, block.field).display()}")
                )
            case _:
                raise UnsupportedContentError(type(block).__name__)


def _render_table(writer: _Writer, chapter: ChapterInput, ctx: RenderContext) -> None:
    content = chapter.content
    if not isinstance(content, TableContent):
        raise UnsupportedContentError(chapter.key)
    writer.table([_bold(c) for c in content.columns], content.rows)


def _render_stories(
    writer: _Writer, chapter: ChapterInput, ctx: RenderContext
) -> None:
    content = chapter.content
    if not isinstance(content, StoriesContent):
        raise UnsupportedContentError(chapter.key)
    stories = [s for s in ctx.stories if s.scope in content.scopes]
    if not stories:
        writer.paragraph(_text(NO_STORIES_TEXT))
        return
    heading_level = min(chapter.level + 1, 4)
    for group, items in groupby(stories, key=lambda s: s.group or NO_GROUP_LABEL):
        writer.heading(group, heading_level)
        for story in items:
            label = SCOPE_LABELS.get(story.scope, story.scope)
            head = _bold(f"{story.key} – {story.title}")
            head.extend(_text(f" ({label})"))
            writer.paragraph(head)
            writer.paragraph(_text(story.sentence))


def _render_calc(writer: _Writer, chapter: ChapterInput, ctx: RenderContext) -> None:
    content = chapter.content
    if not isinstance(content, CalcContent):
        raise UnsupportedContentError(chapter.key)
    if content.intro:
        writer.paragraph(content.intro)
    rows = [
        [_text(row.label), _text(_resolve(ctx, row.field).display())]
        for row in content.rows
    ]
    writer.table([_bold("Position"), _bold("Wert")], rows)


def _plain(runs: Inline) -> str:
    return "".join(run.text for run in runs)


RENDERERS: dict[str, Renderer] = {
    "prose": _render_prose,
    "table": _render_table,
    "stories": _render_stories,
    "calc": _render_calc,
}

chapters from typed content. The story map graphic is never rendered."""

from __future__ import annotations

import io
from collections.abc import Sequence

from docx import Document
from docxtpl import DocxTemplate

from alloq_offer.workshop.content.schema import Run
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.chapter_renderers import RENDERERS, _Writer
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.models import (
    ChapterInput,
    RenderContext,
    UnsupportedContentError,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.template_package import (
    CHAPTER_ANCHOR,
    TemplatePackage,
)

DRAFT_MARKER = "ENTWURF – nicht zur Weitergabe an den Kunden"


def render_document(
    package: TemplatePackage,
    chapters: Sequence[ChapterInput],
    ctx: RenderContext,
) -> bytes:
    template = DocxTemplate(io.BytesIO(package.layout_bytes()))
    template.render(dict(ctx.cover))
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    template.save(buffer)
    buffer.seek(0)

    document = Document(buffer)
    anchor = next(p for p in document.paragraphs if p.text.strip() == CHAPTER_ANCHOR)
    writer = _Writer(document, anchor)
    if ctx.draft:
        writer.paragraph([Run(text=DRAFT_MARKER, bold=True)])
    for chapter in chapters:
        renderer = RENDERERS.get(chapter.content.chapter_type)
        if renderer is None:
            raise UnsupportedContentError(chapter.content.chapter_type)
        writer.heading(chapter.title, chapter.level)
        renderer(writer, chapter, ctx)
    anchor._p.getparent().remove(anchor._p)  # noqa: SLF001

    out = io.BytesIO()
    document.save(out)
    return out.getvalue()

import io
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from docx import Document
from docx.oxml.ns import qn

from alloq_offer.workshop.content.schema import (
    BoundValue,
    BulletList,
    CalcContent,
    CalcRow,
    Heading,
    OrderedList,
    Paragraph,
    ProseContent,
    Run,
    StoriesContent,
    TableBlock,
    TableContent,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.docx_renderer import DRAFT_MARKER, render_document
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.models import (
    MISSING_MARK,
    UNCONFIRMED_MARK,
    ChapterInput,
    RenderContext,
    RenderError,
    ResolvedStory,
    ResolvedValue,
    UnsupportedContentError,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.template_package import load_template

SPECIAL = "Größe <b> & „Zitat“ 5 € \x0b"
SAMPLE_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "docs" / "features" / "offer-workshop-sample.docx"


def _runs(text: str, bold: bool = False) -> list[Run]:
    return [Run(text=text, bold=bold)]


def _chapters() -> list[ChapterInput]:
    wide = TableBlock(
        header=[_runs(f"Spalte {i}") for i in range(8)],
        rows=[[_runs(f"{r}-{c}") for c in range(8)] for r in range(3)],
    )
    prose = ProseContent(
        blocks=[
            Paragraph(runs=_runs("Langer Text " * 200) + _runs(SPECIAL, bold=True)),
            Heading(level=3, runs=_runs("Unterpunkt")),
            BulletList(items=[_runs("Punkt A"), _runs("Punkt B")]),
            OrderedList(items=[_runs("Schritt 1"), _runs("Schritt 2")]),
            wide,
            BoundValue(field="offer.recommended_price"),
        ]
    )
    return [
        ChapterInput("management_summary", "Management Summary", 1, prose),
        ChapterInput(
            "user_stories",
            "Angebotene User Stories",
            2,
            StoriesContent(scopes=["angeboten"], group_by="activity"),
        ),
        ChapterInput(
            "mitwirkung",
            "Mitwirkungspflichten",
            2,
            TableContent(columns=["Mitwirkung", "Wer"], rows=[[_runs("Zugang"), _runs("Kunde")]]),
        ),
        ChapterInput(
            "verguetung",
            "Vergütung",
            1,
            CalcContent(
                intro=_runs("Kalkulation:"),
                rows=[
                    CalcRow(label="Preis", field="offer.recommended_price"),
                    CalcRow(label="Tage", field="offer.person_days"),
                    CalcRow(label="Kosten", field="offer.production_cost"),
                ],
            ),
        ),
    ]


def _context(draft: bool = True) -> RenderContext:
    stories = [
        ResolvedStory(
            key=f"US-{i:02d}",
            title=f"Story {i}",
            sentence=f"Als Rolle möchte ich Ziel {i}, um Nutzen zu haben.",
            scope="angeboten" if i % 5 else "option",
            group=f"Aktivität {i // 10 + 1}",
        )
        for i in range(1, 41)
    ]
    return RenderContext(
        cover={
            "project_title": "Projekt <Ä>",
            "customer_name": "Kunde GmbH",
            "customer_street": "Straße 1",
            "customer_city": "12345 Stadt",
            "customer_short": "Kunde",
            "offer_date": "1. Januar 2027",
            "quote_id": "QUO-1",
            "validity_date": "1. März 2027",
        },
        stories=stories,
        values={
            "offer.recommended_price": ResolvedValue("10.000 €", confirmed=True),
            "offer.person_days": ResolvedValue("12", confirmed=False),
        },
        draft=draft,
    )


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def rendered() -> bytes:
    return render_document(load_template(), _chapters(), _context())


def _doc(data: bytes) -> Document:
    return Document(io.BytesIO(data))


def test_cover_and_tail_are_filled(rendered: bytes) -> None:
    text = "\n".join(p.text for p in _doc(rendered).paragraphs)
    assert "Projekt <Ä>" in text
    assert "Kunde GmbH" in text
    assert "Leipzig, 1. Januar 2027" in text
    assert "bis einschließlich zum 1. März 2027" in text
    assert "{{" not in text
    assert "[[KAPITEL]]" not in text


def test_chapter_order_and_headings(rendered: bytes) -> None:
    doc = _doc(rendered)
    headings = [
        (p.style.name, p.text)
        for p in doc.paragraphs
        if p.style.name.startswith("Heading")
    ]
    titles = [t for _, t in headings]
    order = [
        "Management Summary",
        "Angebotene User Stories",
        "Mitwirkungspflichten",
        "Vergütung",
        "Rechtliche Bestimmungen",
    ]
    positions = [titles.index(t) for t in order]
    assert positions == sorted(positions)
    assert ("Heading 2", "Angebotene User Stories") in headings
    assert ("Heading 3", "Unterpunkt") in headings


def test_prose_blocks_and_special_characters(rendered: bytes) -> None:
    doc = _doc(rendered)
    text = "\n".join(p.text for p in doc.paragraphs)
    assert "Größe <b> & „Zitat“ 5 €" in text
    styles = {p.style.name for p in doc.paragraphs}
    assert {"Aufzählung 1", "List Number"} <= styles
    wide = next(t for t in doc.tables if t.rows[0].cells[0].text == "Spalte 0")
    assert len(wide.columns) == 8
    assert wide.style.name == "arvato-Tabelle blau"
    assert wide.rows[3].cells[7].text == "2-7"


def test_stories_chapter_written_stories_grouped(rendered: bytes) -> None:
    doc = _doc(rendered)

    assert "Als Rolle möchte ich Ziel 1, um Nutzen zu haben." in texts
    assert not any(t.startswith("US-05 ") for t in texts)  # scope option filtered out
    assert "Aktivität 1" in texts and "Aktivität 5" in texts


def test_calc_marks_unconfirmed_and_missing(rendered: bytes) -> None:
    doc = _doc(rendered)
    calc = next(t for t in doc.tables if t.rows[0].cells[0].text == "Position")
    cells = {r.cells[0].text: r.cells[1].text for r in calc.rows[1:]}
    assert cells["Preis"] == "10.000 €"
    assert cells["Tage"] == f"12 {UNCONFIRMED_MARK}"
    assert cells["Kosten"] == MISSING_MARK


def test_draft_marker_toc_and_no_map(rendered: bytes) -> None:
    doc = _doc(rendered)
    assert any(p.text == DRAFT_MARKER for p in doc.paragraphs)

        render_document(load_template(), [bad], _context())

# Offer workshop template (QUO)

The workshop fills the customer template `Templates/QUO-33441-N7R0Z4_Preisindikation MVP Referenzdatenbank Treystar .docx`.
`scripts/inventory_docx.py` prints its structure; `scripts/build_quo_layout.py` turns it into the package layout.

## What is fixed and what is generated

| Part | Source in the QUO file | In the package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cover (title, customer, date, quote id) | paragraphs 0 to 25 | `layout.docx` with `{{ project_title }}`, `{{ customer_name }}`, `{{ customer_street }}`, `{{ customer_city }}`, `{{ customer_short }}`, `{{ offer_date }}`, `{{ quote_id }}` |
| Legal notice, supplier address | cover | fixed text |
| Table of contents | missing in the QUO file | TOC field `1-3`, updated when Word opens the file |
| Chapters Management Summary to Consumption | Heading 1 to 3 | removed from the layout, rendered from typed chapters at the anchor `[[KAPITEL]]` |
| Rechtliche Bestimmungen, Bindefrist (`{{ validity_date }}`), Sonstiges, Anlagen, Unterschriften | tail | fixed text; signature placeholders (`$$_PRT_..._$$`) stay untouched |

Customer data is removed from the layout. There is no story map chapter: the document shows written stories only.

## Chapters (`chapters.yaml`)

| Key | Level | Type | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `management_summary` | 1 | prose | yes |
| `leistungen` | 1 | prose | no |
| `user_stories` | 2 | stories (angeboten + option, grouped by activity) | yes |
| `loesung` | 2 | prose | yes |
| `leistungsumfang` | 2 | prose | yes |
| `mitwirkung` | 2 | table (Mitwirkung, Verantwortlich, Zeitpunkt) | yes |
| `rahmenbedingungen` | 2 | prose | no |
| `projektabwicklung` | 1 | prose | no |
| `laufzeit` | 1 | prose | yes |
| `verguetung` | 1 | calc (person days, risk buffer, production cost, recommended price) | yes |
| `annahmen_risiken` | 1 | prose | no |

The consumption chapter of the QUO file is not part of Etappe 1.

## Word styles used by the renderer

| Content | Style |
| --- | --- |
| Chapter titles | `Heading 1` and `Heading 2` (style ids `berschrift1`, `berschrift2`) |
| Headings inside a chapter | `Heading 3`, `Heading 4`, never above the chapter level |
| Text | `Normal` |
| Bullet list | `Aufzählung 1` |
| Ordered list | `List Number` |
| Tables | table style `arvato-Tabelle blau`, header row repeats |

## Rendering rules

- Content is rendered by one renderer per chapter type; unknown content raises a typed error and is never dropped.
- `stories` chapters list the stories of the bound map revision: a heading per group, then key, title and scope, then the one sentence "Als … möchte ich …, um …".
- `calc` values are shown only when confirmed; an unconfirmed value carries `[nicht bestätigt]`, a missing one `[Wert fehlt]`.
- A draft export starts with the marker "ENTWURF – nicht zur Weitergabe an den Kunden".
- `docs/features/offer-workshop-sample.docx` is a reference export for the manual check in Word.

# Offer workshop template (QUO)

The workshop fills the customer template `Templates/QUO-33441-N7R0Z4_Preisindikation MVP Referenzdatenbank Treystar .docx`.

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

  Efficiency review of the staged workshop changes. Base path: /Users/jens/Workspace/work/alloq/components/alloq-offer. I found 6 low-impact items and no hot-path problems. Nothing runs per request in a loop.
  
  1. src/alloq_offer/workshop/export/template_package.py:85 and :61-68 (`load_template` calling `check_layout`). Every `load_template()` call parses the full layout.docx with python-docx just to count anchors. `render_document` then parses it again, twice (docxtpl, then `Document` on the saved buffer). Cheaper: cache `load_template` per (key, root) with `functools.cache`. Alternatively, do the anchor check against the already-rendered document, or only in a test or startup check.
  
  2. src/alloq_offer/workshop/export/docx_renderer.py:32-38. The layout is rendered with docxtpl, saved to a BytesIO, then reparsed with `Document(buffer)`. This is a full serialize and parse round trip. Cheaper: use `template.docx` (the python-docx document inside the DocxTemplate) after `template.render(...)`, with no save and reopen. The anchor and Writer can work on that object directly.
  
  3. src/alloq_offer/workshop/export/template_package.py:58-59 (`layout_bytes`). The layout file is re-read from disk on every call. It is called in `check_layout` and again in `render_document`. Cheaper: cache the bytes on the package, for example with `functools.cached_property` or a private attribute.
  
  4. src/alloq_offer/workshop/export/chapter_renderers.py:52-56 and :68, :74 (`Writer._style`). Each paragraph and heading does a style lookup by name with a try/except. `table()` does it as well. Cheaper: memoize resolved style names in a dict on the Writer, or resolve the few fixed styles once in `__init__`. The gain is small.
  
  5. src/alloq_offer/workshop/export/chapter_renderers.py:68 and :74. `self._doc.add_paragraph(...)` appends the paragraph at the end of the body, and `_place` then moves it in front of the anchor. Each paragraph is created and moved. The same happens in `table()` with `add_table`. Cheaper: build the element and insert it with `anchor._p.addprevious` directly, or bulk-build the XML. This is low priority because the cost is small.
  
  6. tests/test_workshop_docx_renderer.py:210, :217, :224 and tests/test_workshop_template.py:16, :30, :40, :49. `load_template()` is called repeatedly in tests, and each call parses the layout. The module-scoped `rendered` fixture is good. Cheaper: add a module-scoped `package` fixture. Note that `test_duplicate_chapter_keys_rejected` may mutate the package, so it needs its own copy. Fixing finding 1 would also remove most of this cost.
  
  scripts/build_quo_layout.py and scripts/inventory_docx.py: none. Both are one-off CLI scripts. The only repeated work is minor, such as `text_of(paragraph)` called twice per paragraph at build_quo_layout.py:138 and :148, and inventory_docx.py:21 indexing `doc.paragraphs`, which rebuilds the list on every iteration and is quadratic in paragraph count. That only matters for large documents. A quick fix would be to drop the unused `para` lookup at lines 21 and 29, since it is deleted immediately.

"""Typed chapter content model of the offer workshop.

A chapter holds one of four content types. ``prose`` is the canonical block
tree, ``table`` a plain grid, ``stories`` only settings (the text is resolved
from the story map when rendering) and ``calc`` bound commercial values.
Anything outside this model is rejected with a German message.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from pydantic import (
    BaseModel,
    Field,
    TypeAdapter,
    ValidationError,
    ValidationInfo,
    field_validator,
)
from pydantic_core import ErrorDetails

STORY_SCOPES: tuple[str, ...] = ("offen", "angeboten", "option", "ausgeschlossen")
GROUP_BY_VALUES: tuple[str, ...] = ("activity", "slice")

BOUND_FIELDS: dict[str, str] = {
    "offer.person_days": "Personentage",
    "offer.risk_buffer_days": "Risikopuffer (Personentage)",
    "offer.production_cost": "Herstellkosten",
    "offer.recommended_price": "Empfohlener Preis",
    "workspace.currency": "Währung",
    "workspace.validity_date": "Bindefrist",
}


class ContentValidationError(ValueError):
    """Chapter content violates the content model; messages are German."""

    def __init__(self, messages: list[str]) -> None:

    def runs(self, paragraph: DocxParagraph, runs: Inline) -> None:
        for run in runs:
            target = paragraph.add_run(_ILLEGAL_XML.sub("", run.text))
            target.bold = run.bold or None
            target.italic = run.italic or None

    def paragraph(self, runs: Inline, style: str | None = None) -> DocxParagraph:
        paragraph = self._doc.add_paragraph(style=self._style(style) if style else None)
        self.runs(paragraph, runs)
        self._place(paragraph._p)  # noqa: SLF001

content.text:
`high effort → 8 inline angles → dedup (no verify) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** in sequence yourself, in THIS context — do NOT spawn subagents for them. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates are the dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Dedup only (no verify)

Pool all candidates. Dedup near-duplicates only (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). Do NOT run verifiers; do NOT re-judge. Sort by severity.

## Output

Target **at least 5 findings**. If fewer genuine findings exist, emit what you have — do not invent to hit the floor.

Call the ReportFindings tool once to report this review's results

"""Offer and industry entities and the offer state enum."""

import enum
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

from sqlalchemy import Boolean, Date, ForeignKey, Index, Numeric, String
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from sqlalchemy.sql import false

from appkit_commons.database.entities import Base, Entity


class OfferStateEnum(enum.StrEnum):
    """State labels of an offer."""

    NEW = "Neu"
    IN_PROGRESS = "In Bearbeitung"
    SENT = "Versendet"


class IndustryEntity(Entity, Base):
    """Customer industry (Branche) of an offer; admins maintain the list."""

    __tablename__ = "industries"

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(100), unique=True, nullable=False)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        """Convert entity to dictionary for Pydantic model creation."""
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "name": self.name,
            "created": self.created,
            "updated": self.updated,
        }


class OfferEntity(Entity, Base):
    """Offer calculated for a customer project."""

    __tablename__ = "offers"
    __table_args__ = (Index("ix_offers_state", "state"),)
