tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: small — keep workflows under 5 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

"""Async repositories of the offer workshop."""

from sqlalchemy import delete, func, select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import (
    JobEntity,
    SourceBlockEntity,
    SourceEntity,
    WorkspaceEntity,
)
from appkit_commons.database.base_repository import BaseRepository


class WorkspaceRepository(BaseRepository[WorkspaceEntity, AsyncSession]):
    """Reads and writes the workshop workspace of an offer."""

    @property
    def model_class(self) -> type[WorkspaceEntity]:
        return WorkspaceEntity

    async def find_by_offer(
        self, session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int
    ) -> WorkspaceEntity | None:
        return await session.scalar(
            select(WorkspaceEntity).where(WorkspaceEntity.offer_id == offer_id)
        )


class JobRepository(BaseRepository[JobEntity, AsyncSession]):
    """Reads workshop jobs; writes go through ``workshop.jobs.queue``."""

    @property
    def model_class(self) -> type[JobEntity]:
        return JobEntity

    async def count_of_kind(
        self, session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, kind: str
    ) -> int:
        return (
            await session.scalar(
                select(func.count())
                .select_from(JobEntity)
                .where(JobEntity.offer_id == offer_id, JobEntity.kind == kind)
            )
            or 0
        )

    async def find_latest(
        self, session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, kind: str
    ) -> JobEntity | None:
        return await session.scalar(
            select(JobEntity)
            .where(JobEntity.offer_id == offer_id, JobEntity.kind == kind)
            .order_by(JobEntity.id.desc())
            .limit(1)
        )


class SourceRepository(BaseRepository[SourceEntity, AsyncSession]):
    """Reads the customer sources of an offer; revoked sources never show up."""

    @property
    def model_class(self) -> type[SourceEntity]:
        return SourceEntity

    async def find_in_offer(
        self, session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, source_id: int
    ) -> SourceEntity | None:
        return await session.scalar(
            select(SourceEntity).where(
                SourceEntity.id == source_id, SourceEntity.offer_id == offer_id
            )
        )

    async def find_by_sha(
        self, session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, sha256: str
    ) -> SourceEntity | None:
        return await session.scalar(
            select(SourceEntity)
            .where(
                SourceEntity.offer_id == offer_id,
                SourceEntity.sha256 == sha256,
                SourceEntity.revoked_at.is_(None),
            )
            .order_by(SourceEntity.id.desc())
            .limit(1)
        )

    async def find_latest_by_filename(
        self, session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, filename: str
    ) -> SourceEntity | None:
        return await session.scalar(
            select(SourceEntity)
            .where(
                SourceEntity.offer_id == offer_id,
                SourceEntity.filename == filename,
                SourceEntity.revoked_at.is_(None),
            )
            .order_by(SourceEntity.version.desc())
            .limit(1)
        )

    async def list_current(
        self, session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int
    ) -> list[SourceEntity]:
        """Sources that are neither revoked nor replaced by a newer version."""
        rows = (
            await session.scalars(
                select(SourceEntity)
                .where(
                    SourceEntity.offer_id == offer_id,
                    SourceEntity.revoked_at.is_(None),
                )
                .order_by(SourceEntity.id)
            )
        ).all()
        replaced = {row.replaces_id for row in rows if row.replaces_id is not None}
        return [row for row in rows if row.id not in replaced]


class SourceBlockRepository(BaseRepository[SourceBlockEntity, AsyncSession]):
    """Reads and replaces the extracted blocks of a source."""

    @property
    def model_class(self) -> type[SourceBlockEntity]:
        return SourceBlockEntity

    async def list_for_source(
        self, session: AsyncSession, source_id: int
    ) -> list[SourceBlockEntity]:
        return list(
            (
                await session.scalars(
                    select(SourceBlockEntity)
                    .where(SourceBlockEntity.source_id == source_id)
                    .order_by(SourceBlockEntity.seq)
                )
            ).all()
        )

    async def replace(
        self,
        session: AsyncSession,
        source_id: int,
        blocks: list[SourceBlockEntity],
    ) -> None:
        await session.execute(
            delete(SourceBlockEntity).where(SourceBlockEntity.source_id == source_id)
        )
        session.add_all(blocks)


workspace_repo = WorkspaceRepository()
job_repo = JobRepository()
source_repo = SourceRepository()
source_block_repo = SourceBlockRepository()

import logging
from functools import cache
from importlib import resources

import httpx
from pydantic_ai import Agent
from pydantic_ai.exceptions import ModelHTTPError, UnexpectedModelBehavior
from pydantic_ai.models import Model
from pydantic_ai.models.openai import OpenAIChatModel
from pydantic_ai.providers.azure import AzureProvider
from pydantic_ai.settings import ModelSettings
from pydantic_ai.usage import UsageLimits

from alloq_offer.workshop.ai.port import (
    AiTransientError,
    AiUnavailableError,
    SourceText,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.ai.render import render_sources
from alloq_offer.workshop.ai.schemas import ProposedBriefing, ProposedMap
from alloq_offer.workshop.configuration import WorkshopConfig

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAP_PROMPT = "map_v1"
BRIEFING_PROMPT = "briefing_v1"
NOT_CONFIGURED = "Die KI ist nicht eingerichtet."
RATE_LIMITED = 429
SERVER_ERROR = 500


@cache
def load_prompt(name: str) -> str:
    return (
        resources.files("alloq_offer.workshop.ai.prompts")
        .joinpath(f"{name}.md")
        .read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )


def build_azure_model(config: WorkshopConfig) -> Model:
    azure = config.azure_openai
    if not (azure.endpoint and azure.chat_deployment):
        raise AiUnavailableError(NOT_CONFIGURED)
    provider = AzureProvider(
        azure_endpoint=azure.endpoint,
        api_version=azure.api_version,
        api_key=REDACTED,
    )
    return OpenAIChatModel(azure.chat_deployment, provider=provider)


class PydanticOfferAi:
    """Proposals from a pydantic-ai model; outputs are validated or retried."""

    map_prompt_version = MAP_PROMPT
    briefing_prompt_version = BRIEFING_PROMPT

    def __init__(self, model: Model, config: WorkshopConfig, name: str) -> None:
        self._model = model
        self._config = config
        self.model_name = name

    async def _run[T](
        self, output: type[T], prompt: str, user_prompt: str, label: str
    ) -> T:
        agent = Agent(
            self._model,
            name=label,
            output_type=output,
            instructions=load_prompt(prompt),
            retries=2,
            model_settings=ModelSettings(timeout=self._config.ai_timeout_seconds),
        )
        try:
            result = await agent.run(
                user_prompt,
                usage_limits=UsageLimits(request_limit=self._config.ai_request_limit),
            )
        except ModelHTTPError as exc:
            if exc.status_code == RATE_LIMITED or exc.status_code >= SERVER_ERROR:
                raise AiTransientError(label) from exc
            raise AiUnavailableError(label) from exc
        except (httpx.TransportError, TimeoutError) as exc:
            raise AiTransientError(label) from exc
        except UnexpectedModelBehavior as exc:
            raise AiUnavailableError(label) from exc
        logger.info("Model run %s used %s", label, result.usage)
        return result.output

    async def propose_map(self, sources: list[SourceText]) -> ProposedMap:
        data = render_sources(sources, self._config.ai_max_input_chars)
        return await self._run(ProposedMap, MAP_PROMPT, data, "propose_map")

    async def propose_briefing(self, sources: list[SourceText]) -> ProposedBriefing:
        data = render_sources(sources, self._config.ai_max_input_chars)
        return await self._run(
            ProposedBriefing, BRIEFING_PROMPT, data, "propose_briefing"
        )


def create_offer_ai(config: WorkshopConfig) -> PydanticOfferAi:
    return PydanticOfferAi(
        build_azure_model(config), config, config.azure_openai.chat_deployment
    )

"""Sources as clearly delimited data for a prompt."""

from alloq_offer.workshop.ai.port import SourceText

TRUNCATED = "[Weitere Quellen wurden wegen der Länge ausgelassen.]"


def _escape(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("</quelle>", "<\\/quelle>").replace("<quelle", "<\\quelle")


def render_sources(sources: list[SourceText], max_chars: int) -> str:
    """One ``<quelle>`` block per source; whole sources are dropped past the budget."""
    parts: list[str] = []
    used = 0
    for source in sources:
        lines = [f'<quelle id="{source.id}" art="{_escape(source.kind)}">']
        lines.append(f"Titel: {_escape(source.title)}")
        for block in source.blocks:
            speaker = f"{block.speaker}: " if block.speaker else ""
            label = f" ({block.label})" if block.label else ""
            lines.append(f"[B{block.id}]{label} {speaker}{_escape(block.text)}")
        lines.extend(f"[Lücke] {_escape(gap)}" for gap in source.gaps)
        lines.append("</quelle>")
        text = "\n".join(lines)
        if parts and used + len(text) > max_chars:
            parts.append(TRUNCATED)
            break
        parts.append(text)
        used += len(text)
    return "\n\n".join(parts)
"""Job ``initial_draft``: sources to story map and briefing in one pass (spec 9.1)."""

import asyncio
import logging

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.ai.agents import create_offer_ai
from alloq_offer.workshop.ai.port import (
    AiTransientError,
    AiUnavailableError,
    BlockText,
    OfferAi,
    SourceText,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.configuration import WorkshopConfig
from alloq_offer.workshop.db import SessionFactory
from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import (
    GenerationRunEntity,
    SourceKind,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.extraction.models import KIND_GAP, anchor_label
from alloq_offer.workshop.jobs.registry import (
    JobContext,
    PermanentJobError,
    TransientJobError,
    register_handler,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.repositories import (
    source_block_repo,
    source_repo,
    workspace_repo,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.map_apply import apply_briefing, apply_proposed_map
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.sources import (
    INITIAL_DRAFT_JOB,
    READABLE_STATUSES,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.workspace import open_workspace
from appkit_commons.database.session import get_asyncdb_session
from appkit_commons.registry import service_registry

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

AI_FAILED = "Die KI konnte keinen Entwurf liefern. Bitte prüfen Sie die Einrichtung."
AI_BUSY = "Die KI ist gerade nicht erreichbar. Der Auftrag wird erneut versucht."
KIND_NAMES = {
    SourceKind.EML: "E-Mail",
    SourceKind.AUDIO: "Mitschnitt",
    SourceKind.PPTX: "Folien",
}


class InitialDraft:
    """Builds the first map; an existing map is never touched by the model."""

    def __init__(self, ai: OfferAi, session_factory: SessionFactory) -> None:
        self._ai = ai
        self._session_factory = session_factory

    async def run(self, ctx: JobContext) -> dict:
        loaded = await self._load(ctx.offer_id)
        if loaded is None:
            return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "map exists or no sources"}
        sources, valid_ids = loaded
        try:
            proposed, briefing = await asyncio.gather(
                self._ai.propose_map(sources), self._ai.propose_briefing(sources)
            )
        except AiTransientError as exc:
            await self._record_run(ctx, sources, "wiederholt")
            raise TransientJobError(AI_BUSY) from exc
        except AiUnavailableError as exc:
            await self._record_run(ctx, sources, "fehlgeschlagen")
            raise PermanentJobError(AI_FAILED) from exc
        async with self._session_factory() as session:
            workspace = await open_workspace(session, ctx.offer_id, "")
            # Lock the row: a second run must wait and then see the new map.
            await session.refresh(workspace, with_for_update=True)
            if workspace.map_revision > 0:
                return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "map exists"}
            applied = await apply_proposed_map(session, workspace, proposed, valid_ids)
            statements = await apply_briefing(
                session, ctx.offer_id, briefing, valid_ids
            )
            self._add_run(session, ctx, sources, "ok")
        logger.info(
            "Initial draft of offer %s: %d stories, %d skipped",
            ctx.offer_id,
            applied.stories,
            len(applied.skipped),
        )
        return {
            "status": "ok",
            "stories": applied.stories,
            "skipped": len(applied.skipped),
            "statements": applied.statements + statements,
        }

    def _add_run(
        self,
        session: AsyncSession,
        ctx: JobContext,
        sources: list[SourceText],
        status: str,
    ) -> None:
        session.add(
            GenerationRunEntity(
                offer_id=ctx.offer_id,
                job_id=ctx.job_id,
                kind=INITIAL_DRAFT_JOB,
                model=self._ai.model_name,
                prompt_version=(
                    f"{self._ai.map_prompt_version}+{self._ai.briefing_prompt_version}"
                ),
                input_revisions={"sources": [source.id for source in sources]},
                status=status,
            )
        )

    async def _record_run(
        self, ctx: JobContext, sources: list[SourceText], status: str
    ) -> None:
        async with self._session_factory() as session:
            self._add_run(session, ctx, sources, status)

    async def _load(self, offer_id: int) -> tuple[list[SourceText], set[int]] | None:
        async with self._session_factory() as session:
            workspace = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
            if workspace is not None and workspace.map_revision > 0:
                return None
            sources: list[SourceText] = []
            valid_ids: set[int] = set()
            for source in await source_repo.list_current(session, offer_id):
                if not source.included or source.status not in READABLE_STATUSES:
                    continue
                blocks = await source_block_repo.list_for_source(session, source.id)
                texts = [
                    BlockText(b.id, b.text, anchor_label(b.anchor), b.speaker)
                    for b in blocks
                    if b.kind != KIND_GAP
                ]
                valid_ids.update(block.id for block in texts)
                sources.append(
                    SourceText(
                        id=source.id,
                        title=source.title,
                        kind=KIND_NAMES.get(SourceKind(source.kind), "Dokument"),
                        blocks=texts,
                        gaps=[b.text for b in blocks if b.kind == KIND_GAP],
                    )
                )
        return (sources, valid_ids) if sources else None


@register_handler(INITIAL_DRAFT_JOB)
async def initial_draft(ctx: JobContext) -> dict:
    config = service_registry().get(WorkshopConfig)
    return await InitialDraft(create_offer_ai(config), get_asyncdb_session).run(ctx)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAP_PROMPT = "map_v1"
BRIEFING_PROMPT = "briefing_v1"
NOT_CONFIGURED = "Die KI ist nicht eingerichtet."
RATE_LIMITED = 429
SERVER_ERROR = 500


@cache
def load_prompt(name: str) -> str:
    return (
        resources.files("alloq_offer.workshop.ai.prompts")
        .joinpath(f"{name}.md")
        .read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    )


def build_azure_model(config: WorkshopConfig) -> Model:
    azure = config.azure_openai
    if not (azure.endpoint and azure.chat_deployment):
        raise AiUnavailableError(NOT_CONFIGURED)
    provider = AzureProvider(
        azure_endpoint=azure.endpoint,
        api_version=azure.api_version,
        api_key=REDACTED,
    )
    return OpenAIChatModel(azure.chat_deployment, provider=provider)


class PydanticOfferAi:
    """Proposals from a pydantic-ai model; outputs are validated or retried."""

    map_prompt_version = MAP_PROMPT
    briefing_prompt_version = BRIEFING_PROMPT

    def __init__(self, model: Model, config: WorkshopConfig, name: str) -> None:
        self._model = model
        self._config = config
        self.model_name = name

    async def _run[T](
        self, output: type[T], prompt: str, user_prompt: str, label: str
    ) -> T:
        agent = Agent(
            self._model,
            name=label,
            output_type=output,
            instructions=load_prompt(prompt),
            retries=2,
            model_settings=ModelSettings(timeout=self._config.ai_timeout_seconds),
        )
        try:
            result = await agent.run(
                user_prompt,
                usage_limits=UsageLimits(request_limit=self._config.ai_request_limit),
            )
        except ModelHTTPError as exc:
            if exc.status_code == RATE_LIMITED or exc.status_code >= SERVER_ERROR:
                raise AiTransientError(label) from exc
            raise AiUnavailableError(label) from exc
        except (httpx.TransportError, TimeoutError) as exc:
            raise AiTransientError(label) from exc
        except UnexpectedModelBehavior as exc:
            raise AiUnavailableError(label) from exc
        logger.info("Model run %s used %s", label, result.usage)
        return result.output

    async def propose_map(self, sources: list[SourceText]) -> ProposedMap:
        data = render_sources(sources, self._config.ai_max_input_chars)
        return await self._run(ProposedMap, MAP_PROMPT, data, "propose_map")

    async def propose_briefing(self, sources: list[SourceText]) -> ProposedBriefing:
        data = render_sources(sources, self._config.ai_max_input_chars)
        return await self._run(
            ProposedBriefing, BRIEFING_PROMPT, data, "propose_briefing"
        )


def create_offer_ai(config: WorkshopConfig) -> PydanticOfferAi:
    return PydanticOfferAi(
        build_azure_model(config), config, config.azure_openai.chat_deployment
    )

"""Sources as clearly delimited data for a prompt."""

from alloq_offer.workshop.ai.port import SourceText

TRUNCATED = "[Weitere Quellen wurden wegen der Länge ausgelassen.]"


def _escape(text: str) -> str:
    return text.replace("</quelle>", "<\\/quelle>").replace("<quelle", "<\\quelle")


def render_sources(sources: list[SourceText], max_chars: int) -> str:
    """One ``<quelle>`` block per source; whole sources are dropped past the budget."""
    parts: list[str] = []
    used = 0
    for source in sources:
        lines = [f'<quelle id="{source.id}" art="{_escape(source.kind)}">']
        lines.append(f"Titel: {_escape(source.title)}")
        for block in source.blocks:
            speaker = f"{block.speaker}: " if block.speaker else ""
            label = f" ({block.label})" if block.label else ""
            lines.append(f"[B{block.id}]{label} {speaker}{_escape(block.text)}")
        lines.extend(f"[Lücke] {_escape(gap)}" for gap in source.gaps)
        lines.append("</quelle>")
        text = "\n".join(lines)
        if parts and used + len(text) > max_chars:
            parts.append(TRUNCATED)
            break
        parts.append(text)
        used += len(text)
    return "\n\n".join(parts)

from alloq_offer.workshop.jobs.registry import (
    JobContext,

    register_handler,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.repositories import (
    source_block_repo,
    source_repo,
    workspace_repo,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.map_apply import apply_briefing, apply_proposed_map
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.sources import (
    INITIAL_DRAFT_JOB,
    READABLE_STATUSES,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.services.workspace import open_workspace
from appkit_commons.database.session import get_asyncdb_session
from appkit_commons.registry import service_registry

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

AI_FAILED = "Die KI konnte keinen Entwurf liefern. Bitte prüfen Sie die Einrichtung."
AI_BUSY = "Die KI ist gerade nicht erreichbar. Der Auftrag wird erneut versucht."
KIND_NAMES = {
    SourceKind.EML: "E-Mail",
    SourceKind.AUDIO: "Mitschnitt",
    SourceKind.PPTX: "Folien",
}


class InitialDraft:
    """Builds the first map; an existing map is never touched by the model."""

    def __init__(self, ai: OfferAi, session_factory: SessionFactory) -> None:
        self._ai = ai
        self._session_factory = session_factory

    async def run(self, ctx: JobContext) -> dict:
        loaded = await self._load(ctx.offer_id)
        if loaded is None:
            return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "map exists or no sources"}
        sources, valid_ids = loaded
        try:
            proposed, briefing = await asyncio.gather(
                self._ai.propose_map(sources), self._ai.propose_briefing(sources)
            )
        except AiTransientError as exc:
            await self._record_run(ctx, sources, "wiederholt")
            raise TransientJobError(AI_BUSY) from exc
        except AiUnavailableError as exc:
            await self._record_run(ctx, sources, "fehlgeschlagen")
            raise PermanentJobError(AI_FAILED) from exc
        async with self._session_factory() as session:
            workspace = await open_workspace(session, ctx.offer_id, "")
            # Lock the row: a second run must wait and then see the new map.
            await session.refresh(workspace, with_for_update=True)
            if workspace.map_revision > 0:
                return {"status": "skipped", "reason": "map exists"}
            applied = await apply_proposed_map(session, workspace, proposed, valid_ids)
            statements = await apply_briefing(
                session, ctx.offer_id, briefing, valid_ids
            )
            self._add_run(session, ctx, sources, "ok")
        logger.info(
            "Initial draft of offer %s: %d stories, %d skipped",
            ctx.offer_id,
            applied.stories,
            len(applied.skipped),
        )
        return {
            "status": "ok",
            "stories": applied.stories,
            "skipped": len(applied.skipped),
            "statements": applied.statements + statements,
        }

    def _add_run(
        self,
        session: AsyncSession,
        ctx: JobContext,
        sources: list[SourceText],
        status: str,
    ) -> None:
        session.add(
            GenerationRunEntity(
                offer_id=ctx.offer_id,
                job_id=ctx.job_id,
                kind=INITIAL_DRAFT_JOB,
                model=self._ai.model_name,
                prompt_version=(
                    f"{self._ai.map_prompt_version}+{self._ai.briefing_prompt_version}"
                ),
                input_revisions={"sources": [source.id for source in sources]},
                status=status,
            )
        )

    async def _record_run(
        self, ctx: JobContext, sources: list[SourceText], status: str
    ) -> None:
        async with self._session_factory() as session:
            self._add_run(session, ctx, sources, status)

    async def _load(self, offer_id: int) -> tuple[list[SourceText], set[int]] | None:
        async with self._session_factory() as session:
            workspace = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
            if workspace is not None and workspace.map_revision > 0:
                return None
            sources: list[SourceText] = []
            valid_ids: set[int] = set()
            for source in await source_repo.list_current(session, offer_id):
                if not source.included or source.status not in READABLE_STATUSES:
                    continue
                blocks = await source_block_repo.list_for_source(session, source.id)
                texts = [
                    BlockText(b.id, b.text, anchor_label(b.anchor), b.speaker)
                    for b in blocks
                    if b.kind != KIND_GAP
                ]
                valid_ids.update(block.id for block in texts)
                sources.append(
                    SourceText(
                        id=source.id,
                        title=source.title,
                        kind=KIND_NAMES.get(SourceKind(source.kind), "Dokument"),
                        blocks=texts,
                        gaps=[b.text for b in blocks if b.kind == KIND_GAP],
                    )
                )
        return (sources, valid_ids) if sources else None


@register_handler(INITIAL_DRAFT_JOB)
async def initial_draft(ctx: JobContext) -> dict:
    config = service_registry().get(WorkshopConfig)
    return await InitialDraft(create_offer_ai(config), get_asyncdb_session).run(ctx)

def next_story_key(workspace: WorkspaceEntity) -> str:

def _known_refs(refs: list[int], valid_block_ids: set[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Refs that point at a real block; invented ones are dropped."""
    kept = [ref for ref in dict.fromkeys(refs) if ref in valid_block_ids]
    if len(kept) < len(set(refs)):
        logger.warning("Dropped %d unknown source refs", len(set(refs)) - len(kept))

"""The briefing: statements by type, with the places in the sources they rest on."""

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.db import SessionFactory
from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import (
    SourceBlockEntity,
    SourceEntity,
    StatementEntity,
    StatementStatus,
    StatementType,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.extraction.models import anchor_label

TYPE_ORDER = [
    StatementType.REQUIREMENT,
    StatementType.FACT,
    StatementType.SOLUTION,
    StatementType.ASSUMPTION,
    StatementType.OPEN_POINT,
    StatementType.CONFLICT,
]


async def _ref_labels(session: AsyncSession, block_ids: set[int]) -> dict[int, str]:
    if not block_ids:
        return {}
    rows = await session.execute(
        select(SourceBlockEntity.id, SourceBlockEntity.anchor, SourceEntity.title)
        .join(SourceEntity, SourceEntity.id == SourceBlockEntity.source_id)
        .where(SourceBlockEntity.id.in_(block_ids), SourceEntity.revoked_at.is_(None))
    )
    return {
        block_id: ", ".join(filter(None, [title, anchor_label(anchor)]))
        for block_id, anchor, title in rows.all()
    }


async def load_briefing(session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Statement groups in the order of ``TYPE_ORDER``; empty groups are left out."""
    statements = list(
        (
            await session.scalars(
                select(StatementEntity)
                .where(StatementEntity.offer_id == offer_id)
                .order_by(StatementEntity.id)
            )
        ).all()
    )
    labels = await _ref_labels(
        session, {ref for s in statements for ref in s.source_refs}
    )
    groups: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for type_ in TYPE_ORDER:
        items = [
            {
                "id": s.id,
                "text": s.text,
                "confirmed": s.status == StatementStatus.CONFIRMED,
                "recheck": s.needs_recheck,
                "confirmed_by": s.confirmed_by or "",
                "refs": [labels[r] for r in s.source_refs if r in labels],
            }
            for s in statements
            if s.type == type_
        ]
        if items:
            groups.append({"type": type_.value, "items": items})
    return groups


async def set_confirmed(
    session_factory: SessionFactory,
    offer_id: int,
    statement_id: int,
    *,
    confirmed: bool,
    user: str,
    now: datetime,
) -> bool:
    """Confirm a statement as a professional decision, or take that back.

    Only this explicit action changes the status; drafting never confirms (A17).
    """
    async with session_factory() as session:
        statement = await session.get(StatementEntity, statement_id)
        if statement is None or statement.offer_id != offer_id:
            return False
        statement.status = (
            StatementStatus.CONFIRMED if confirmed else StatementStatus.PROPOSED
        )
        statement.confirmed_by = user if confirmed else None
        statement.confirmed_at = now if confirmed else None
        if confirmed:
            statement.needs_recheck = False
        return True

import logging
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

from alloq_offer.workshop.services.story_rules import story_problems, story_sentence

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

@dataclass

    stories: int = 0
    statements: int = 0

def next_story_key(workspace: WorkspaceEntity) -> str:
    """The next story key; the counter only grows, so keys are never reused."""
    workspace.story_seq += 1
    return f"{KEY_PREFIX}{workspace.story_seq:02d}"


def _known_refs(refs: list[int], valid_block_ids: set[int]) -> list[int]:
    """Refs that point at a real block; invented ones are dropped."""
    kept = [ref for ref in dict.fromkeys(refs) if ref in valid_block_ids]
    if len(kept) < len(set(refs)):
        logger.warning("Dropped %d unknown source refs", len(set(refs)) - len(kept))
    return kept

"""The briefing: statements by type, with the places in the sources they rest on."""

from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.db import SessionFactory
from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import (
    SourceBlockEntity,
    SourceEntity,
    StatementEntity,
    StatementStatus,
    StatementType,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.extraction.models import anchor_label

TYPE_ORDER = [
    StatementType.REQUIREMENT,
    StatementType.FACT,
    StatementType.SOLUTION,
    StatementType.ASSUMPTION,
    StatementType.OPEN_POINT,
    StatementType.CONFLICT,
]


async def _ref_labels(session: AsyncSession, block_ids: set[int]) -> dict[int, str]:
    if not block_ids:
        return {}
    rows = await session.execute(
        select(SourceBlockEntity.id, SourceBlockEntity.anchor, SourceEntity.title)
        .join(SourceEntity, SourceEntity.id == SourceBlockEntity.source_id)
        .where(SourceBlockEntity.id.in_(block_ids), SourceEntity.revoked_at.is_(None))
    )
    return {
        block_id: ", ".join(filter(None, [title, anchor_label(anchor)]))
        for block_id, anchor, title in rows.all()
    }


async def load_briefing(session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Statement groups in the order of ``TYPE_ORDER``; empty groups are left out."""
    statements = list(
        (
            await session.scalars(
                select(StatementEntity)
                .where(StatementEntity.offer_id == offer_id)
                .order_by(StatementEntity.id)
            )
        ).all()
    )
    labels = await _ref_labels(
        session, {ref for s in statements for ref in s.source_refs}
    )
    groups: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for type_ in TYPE_ORDER:
        items = [
            {
                "id": s.id,
                "text": s.text,
                "confirmed": s.status == StatementStatus.CONFIRMED,
                "recheck": s.needs_recheck,
                "confirmed_by": s.confirmed_by or "",
                "refs": [labels[r] for r in s.source_refs if r in labels],
            }
            for s in statements
            if s.type == type_
        ]
        if items:
            groups.append({"type": type_.value, "items": items})
    return groups


async def set_confirmed(
    session_factory: SessionFactory,
    offer_id: int,
    statement_id: int,
    *,
    confirmed: bool,
    user: str,
    now: datetime,
) -> bool:
    """Confirm a statement as a professional decision, or take that back.

    Only this explicit action changes the status; drafting never confirms (A17).
    """
    async with session_factory() as session:
        statement = await session.get(StatementEntity, statement_id)
        if statement is None or statement.offer_id != offer_id:
            return False
        statement.status = (
            StatementStatus.CONFIRMED if confirmed else StatementStatus.PROPOSED
        )
        statement.confirmed_by = user if confirmed else None
        statement.confirmed_at = now if confirmed else None
        if confirmed:
            statement.needs_recheck = False
        return True

"""Open the workshop workspace of an offer, creating it on first use."""

from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import WorkspaceEntity
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.template_package import (
    DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY,
    load_template,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.repositories import workspace_repo


async def open_workspace(
    session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, user: str
) -> WorkspaceEntity:
    """The workspace of ``offer_id``; a new one is bound to the current template."""
    existing = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
    if existing is not None:
        return existing
    template = load_template(DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY)
    workspace = WorkspaceEntity(
        offer_id=offer_id,
        template_key=template.key,
        template_version=template.version,
        created_by=user,
    )
    try:
        async with session.begin_nested():
            session.add(workspace)
    except IntegrityError:
        # A second tab created the workspace first.
        found = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
        if found is None:
            raise
        return found
    return workspace
"""The story map as a grid of plain values for the page (from a map snapshot)."""

from typing import Any

NO_SLICE_ID = 0
NO_SLICE_TITLE = "Ohne Umsetzungsschnitt"
ORIGIN_SOURCE = "Quellenstellen"


def _card(story: dict, task_title: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    refs = len(story["source_refs"])
    return {
        "id": story["id"],
        "key": story["key"],
        "title": story["title"],
        "meta": f"{task_title} · {story['scope']} · {story['origin']}",
        "scope": story["scope"],
        "skeleton": story["skeleton"],
        "origin": story["origin"],
        "sentence": story["sentence"],
        "refs": f"{refs} {ORIGIN_SOURCE}" if refs else "ohne Quellenbezug",
    }


def build_view(snapshot: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Columns, slice rows, option lists and a story lookup for the editor."""
    activities = [a for a in snapshot["activities"] if not a["archived"]]
    slices = snapshot["slices"]
    tasks_of = {
        a["id"]: [t for t in a["tasks"] if not t["archived"]] for a in activities
    }
    columns = [
        {
            "id": a["id"],
            "title": a["title"],
            "tasks": " · ".join(t["title"] for t in tasks_of[a["id"]]),
            "task_id": tasks_of[a["id"]][0]["id"] if tasks_of[a["id"]] else 0,
            "first": index == 0,
            "last": index == len(activities) - 1,
        }
        for index, a in enumerate(activities)
    ]

    def cell(activity: dict, slice_id: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
        stories = [
            _card(s, t["title"])
            for t in tasks_of[activity["id"]]
            for s in t["stories"]
            if not s["archived"] and (s["slice_id"] or NO_SLICE_ID) == slice_id
        ]
        first_task = (
            tasks_of[activity["id"]][0]["id"] if tasks_of[activity["id"]] else 0
        )
        return {
            "activity_id": activity["id"],
            "task_id": first_task,
            "stories": stories,
        }

    row_defs = [(s["id"], s["title"], True) for s in slices] + [
        (NO_SLICE_ID, NO_SLICE_TITLE, False)
    ]
    rows = [
        {
            "slice_id": slice_id,
            "title": title,
            "editable": editable,
            "cells": [cell(a, slice_id) for a in activities],
        }
        for slice_id, title, editable in row_defs
    ]
    lookup = {
        str(story["id"]): {
            **_card(story, task["title"]),
            "role": story["role"],
            "goal": story["goal"],
            "benefit": story["benefit"],
            "task_id": str(task["id"]),
            "slice_id": str(story["slice_id"] or NO_SLICE_ID),
        }
        for activity in activities
        for task in tasks_of[activity["id"]]
        for story in task["stories"]
        if not story["archived"]
    }
    return {
        "columns": columns,
        "rows": rows,
        "stories": lookup,
        "story_count": len(lookup),
        "task_options": [
            {"value": str(t["id"]), "label": f"{a['title']} · {t['title']}"}
            for a in activities
            for t in tasks_of[a["id"]]
        ],
        "slice_options": [{"value": str(NO_SLICE_ID), "label": NO_SLICE_TITLE}]
        + [{"value": str(s["id"]), "label": s["title"]} for s in slices],
    }
                ],
            }
            for a in activities
        ],
        "unassigned": [_story_dict(s) for s in stories if s.task_id is None],
    }


def _story_dict(story: StoryEntity) -> dict:
    return {
        "id": story.id,
        "key": story.key,
        "title": story.title,
        "role": story.role,
        "goal": story.goal,
        "benefit": story.benefit,
        "sentence": story_sentence(story.role, story.goal, story.benefit),
        "scope": story.scope,
        "origin": story.origin,
        "slice_id": story.slice_id,
        "skeleton": story.skeleton,
        "source_refs": story.source_refs,
        "archived": story.archived_at is not None,
    }

"""Open the workshop workspace of an offer, creating it on first use."""

from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from alloq_offer.workshop.entities import WorkspaceEntity
from alloq_offer.workshop.export.template_package import (
    DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY,
    load_template,
)
from alloq_offer.workshop.repositories import workspace_repo


async def open_workspace(
    session: AsyncSession, offer_id: int, user: str
) -> WorkspaceEntity:
    """The workspace of ``offer_id``; a new one is bound to the current template."""
    existing = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
    if existing is not None:
        return existing
    template = load_template(DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_KEY)
    workspace = WorkspaceEntity(
        offer_id=offer_id,
        template_key=template.key,
        template_version=template.version,
        created_by=user,
    )
    try:
        async with session.begin_nested():
            session.add(workspace)
    except IntegrityError:
        # A second tab created the workspace first.
        found = await workspace_repo.find_by_offer(session, offer_id)
        if found is None:
            raise
        return found
    return workspace

from typing import Any

NO_SLICE_ID = 0
NO_SLICE_TITLE = "Ohne Umsetzungsschnitt"
ORIGIN_SOURCE = "Quellenstellen"


def _card(story: dict, task_title: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    refs = len(story["source_refs"])
    return {
        "id": story["id"],
        "key": story["key"],
        "title": story["title"],
        "meta": f"{task_title} · {story['scope']} · {story['origin']}",
        "scope": story["scope"],
        "skeleton": story["skeleton"],
        "origin": story["origin"],
        "sentence": story["sentence"],
        "refs": f"{refs} {ORIGIN_SOURCE}" if refs else "ohne Quellenbezug",
    }


def build_view(snapshot: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Columns, slice rows, option lists and a story lookup for the editor."""
    activities = [a for a in snapshot["activities"] if not a["archived"]]
    slices = snapshot["slices"]
    tasks_of = {
        a["id"]: [t for t in a["tasks"] if not t["archived"]] for a in activities
    }
    columns = [
        {
            "id": a["id"],
            "title": a["title"],
            "tasks": " · ".join(t["title"] for t in tasks_of[a["id"]]),
            "task_id": tasks_of[a["id"]][0]["id"] if tasks_of[a["id"]] else 0,
            "first": index == 0,
            "last": index == len(activities) - 1,
        }
        for index, a in enumerate(activities)
    ]

    def cell(activity: dict, slice_id: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
        stories = [
            _card(s, t["title"])
            for t in tasks_of[activity["id"]]
            for s in t["stories"]
            if not s["archived"] and (s["slice_id"] or NO_SLICE_ID) == slice_id
        ]
        first_task = (
            tasks_of[activity["id"]][0]["id"] if tasks_of[activity["id"]] else 0
        )
        return {
            "activity_id": activity["id"],
            "task_id": first_task,
            "stories": stories,
        }

    row_defs = [(s["id"], s["title"], True) for s in slices] + [
        (NO_SLICE_ID, NO_SLICE_TITLE, False)
    ]
    rows = [
        {
            "slice_id": slice_id,
            "title": title,
            "editable": editable,
            "cells": [cell(a, slice_id) for a in activities],
        }
        for slice_id, title, editable in row_defs
    ]
    lookup = {
        str(story["id"]): {
            **_card(story, task["title"]),
            "role": story["role"],
            "goal": story["goal"],
            "benefit": story["benefit"],
            "task_id": str(task["id"]),
            "slice_id": str(story["slice_id"] or NO_SLICE_ID),
        }
        for activity in activities
        for task in tasks_of[activity["id"]]
        for story in task["stories"]
        if not story["archived"]
    }
    return {
        "columns": columns,
        "rows": rows,
        "stories": lookup,
        "story_count": len(lookup),
        "task_options": [
            {"value": str(t["id"]), "label": f"{a['title']} · {t['title']}"}
            for a in activities
            for t in tasks_of[a["id"]]
        ],
        "slice_options": [{"value": str(NO_SLICE_ID), "label": NO_SLICE_TITLE}]
        + [{"value": str(s["id"]), "label": s["title"]} for s in slices],
    }
                ],
            }
            for a in activities
        ],
        "unassigned": [_story_dict(s) for s in stories if s.task_id is None],
    }

        from mantine import EditorToolbarConfig, ToolbarControlGroup

    show_toolbar: bool | None = None

    @classmethod
    def create(
        cls, toolbar_config: EditorToolbarConfig | None = None, **props: Any
    ) -> rx.Component:
        """Create an instance of RichTextEditor.

        Args:
            toolbar_config: Optional toolbar configuration to customize controls.
            **props: Any properties to be passed to the RichTextEditor

        Returns:
            A RichTextEditor instance.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If toolbar_config is a state Var.

        Example:
            ```python
            from mantine import (
                rich_text_editor,
                EditorToolbarConfig,
                ToolbarControlGroup,
            )

            # With default toolbar
            rich_text_editor(content=State.content, on_update=State.update)

            # With custom toolbar using config
            config = EditorToolbarConfig(
                control_groups=[
                    ToolbarControlGroup.BASIC_FORMATTING.value,
                    ToolbarControlGroup.HEADINGS.value,
                ]
            )
            rich_text_editor(content=State.content, toolbar_config=config)

            # With custom height
            rich_text_editor(
                content=State.content, styles={"content": {"minHeight": "300px"}}
            )
            ```
        """
        if toolbar_config is not None:
            if isinstance(toolbar_config, Var):
                msg = "EditorToolbarConfig cannot be a state Var"
                raise ValueError(msg)
            # Extract individual props from config
            config_dict = toolbar_config.model_dump()
            if config_dict.get("control_groups") is not None:
                props["control_groups"] = config_dict["control_groups"]
            if config_dict.get("show_toolbar") is not None:
                props["show_toolbar"] = config_dict["show_toolbar"]
            if config_dict.get("sticky") is not None:
                props["sticky"] = config_dict["sticky"]
            if config_dict.get("sticky_offset") is not None:
                props["sticky_offset"] = config_dict["sticky_offset"]
        return super().create(**props)

from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field


class TransientJobError(RuntimeError):
    """The job may succeed on a later attempt (timeout, rate limit)."""


class PermanentJobError(RuntimeError):
    """The job cannot succeed; the message is ours and shown to users."""


class UnknownJobKindError(LookupError):
    """No handler is registered for the job kind."""

) -> Callable[[JobHandler], JobHandler]:
    """Register ``handler`` for ``kind``; re-registering replaces it.

    permanent error or an expired lease), so the handler's data never stays in a
    "running" state.

        else:

    except KeyError as exc:

    return sorted(_HANDLERS)

def _bold(value: str) -> Inline:
    return [Run(text=value, bold=True)]


def _resolve(ctx: RenderContext, field: str) -> ResolvedValue:
    return ctx.values.get(field, ResolvedValue(text=None))


def _render_prose(writer: Writer, chapter: ChapterInput, ctx: RenderContext) -> None:
    content = chapter.content
    if not isinstance(content, ProseContent):
        raise UnsupportedContentError(chapter.key)
    inner_min = min(chapter.level + 1, 4)
    for block in content.blocks:
        match block:
            case Paragraph():
                writer.paragraph(block.runs)
            case Heading():
                writer.heading(plain_text(block.runs), max(block.level, inner_min))
            case BulletList():
                for item in block.items:
                    writer.paragraph(item, BULLET_STYLE)
            case OrderedList():
                for item in block.items:
                    writer.paragraph(item, ORDERED_STYLE)
            case TableBlock():
                writer.table(block.header, block.rows)
            case BoundValue():
                label = BOUND_FIELDS[block.field]
                writer.paragraph(
                    _text(f"{label}: {_resolve(ctx, block.field).display()}")
                )
            case _:
                raise UnsupportedContentError(type(block).__name__)


def _render_table(writer: Writer, chapter: ChapterInput, _ctx: RenderContext) -> None:
    content = chapter.content
    if not isinstance(content, TableContent):
        raise UnsupportedContentError(chapter.key)
    writer.table([_bold(c) for c in content.columns], content.rows)


def _render_stories(writer: Writer, chapter: ChapterInput, ctx: RenderContext) -> None:
    content = chapter.content
    if not isinstance(content, StoriesContent):
        raise UnsupportedContentError(chapter.key)
    stories = [s for s in ctx.stories if s.scope in content.scopes]
    if not stories:
        writer.paragraph(_text(NO_STORIES_TEXT))
        return
    heading_level = min(chapter.level + 1, 4)
    groups: dict[str, list[ResolvedStory]] = {}
    for story in stories:
        groups.setdefault(story.group or NO_GROUP_LABEL, []).append(story)
    for group, items in groups.items():
        writer.heading(group, heading_level)
        for story in items:
            label = SCOPE_LABELS.get(story.scope, story.scope)
            head = _bold(f"{story.key} – {story.title}")
            head.extend(_text(f" ({label})"))
            writer.paragraph(head)
            writer.paragraph(_text(story.sentence))
